source_arguments.name: RiemannGaussian.mellin_riemannThetaReflection
source_arguments.statement:
theorem mellin_riemannThetaReflection (s : ℂ) :
    mellin riemannThetaReflection s =
      mellin riemannThetaUpper (1 / 2 - s)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem mellin_riemannThetaReflection (s : ℂ) :
    mellin riemannThetaReflection s =
      mellin riemannThetaUpper (1 / 2 - s)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  unfold riemannThetaReflection
  calc
    mellin
        (fun x : ℝ =>
          (x : ℂ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℂ)) •
            riemannThetaUpper (1 / x)) s =
        mellin (fun x : ℝ => riemannThetaUpper (1 / x))
          (s + -(1 / 2 : ℂ)) :=
      mellin_cpow_smul
        (fun x : ℝ => riemannThetaUpper (1 / x)) s
          (-(1 / 2 : ℂ))
    _ = mellin riemannThetaUpper (-(s + -(1 / 2 : ℂ))) := by
      simpa [one_div] using
        mellin_comp_inv riemannThetaUpper (s + -(1 / 2 : ℂ))
    _ = mellin riemannThetaUpper (1 / 2 - s) := by
      congr 2
      ring

source_arguments.name: GaloisForLFunctions.SelbergClass.mellinInv_line_Gamma_eq_exp_neg
source_arguments.statement:
theorem mellinInv_line_Gamma_eq_exp_neg {c x : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hx : 0 < x) :
    mellinInv c Complex.Gamma x = Complex.exp (-(x : ℂ))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem mellinInv_line_Gamma_eq_exp_neg {c x : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hx : 0 < x) :
    mellinInv c Complex.Gamma x = Complex.exp (-(x : ℂ))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let f : ℝ → ℂ := fun y => ((Real.exp (-y) : ℝ) : ℂ)
  have hc' : 0 < ((c : ℂ)).re := by simpa using hc
  have hconv : MellinConvergent f (c : ℂ) := by
    simpa only [f, one_mul] using
      (RHTower.mellinConvergent_exp_neg_mul (m := 1) (by norm_num) hc')
  have hmellinLine (t : ℝ) :
      mellin f ((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I) =
        Complex.Gamma ((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I) := by
    dsimp only [f]
    simp only [Complex.ofReal_exp, Complex.ofReal_neg]
    have h := RHTower.mellin_exp_neg_mul (m := 1) (by norm_num)
      (by simpa using hc' : 0 < (((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I).re))
    simp only [one_mul] at h
    norm_num at h
    exact h
  have hvertical : Complex.VerticalIntegrable (mellin f) c := by
    apply (gamma_verticalIntegrable_of_pos hc).congr
    exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun t => by
      exact (hmellinLine t).symm
  have hcont : ContinuousAt f x := by
    dsimp only [f]
    fun_prop
  have hinv := mellinInv_mellin_eq c f hx hconv hvertical hcont
  calc
    mellinInv c Complex.Gamma x = mellinInv c (mellin f) x := by
      unfold mellinInv
      congr 1
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun t => by
        change ((x : ℂ) ^ (-((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I))) •
            Complex.Gamma ((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I) =
          ((x : ℂ) ^ (-((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I))) •
            mellin f ((c : ℂ) + (t : ℂ) * I)
        congr 1
        exact (hmellinLine t).symm
    _ = f x := hinv
    _ = Complex.exp (-(x : ℂ)) := by
      dsimp only [f]
      rw [Complex.ofReal_exp, Complex.ofReal_neg]

source_arguments.name: mellinInv_mellin_eq
source_arguments.statement:
theorem mellinInv_mellin_eq (σ : ℝ) (f : ℝ → E) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hf : MellinConvergent f σ)
    (hFf : VerticalIntegrable (mellin f) σ) (hfx : ContinuousAt f x) :
    mellinInv σ (mellin f) x = f x
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem mellinInv_mellin_eq (σ : ℝ) (f : ℝ → E) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hf : MellinConvergent f σ)
    (hFf : VerticalIntegrable (mellin f) σ) (hfx : ContinuousAt f x) :
    mellinInv σ (mellin f) x = f x
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let g := fun (u : ℝ) => Real.exp (-σ * u) • f (Real.exp (-u))
  replace hf : Integrable g := by
    rw [MellinConvergent, ← rexp_neg_image_aux, integrableOn_image_iff_integrableOn_abs_deriv_smul
      MeasurableSet.univ rexp_neg_deriv_aux rexp_neg_injOn_aux] at hf
    replace hf : Integrable fun (x : ℝ) ↦ cexp (-↑σ * ↑x) • f (rexp (-x)) := by
      simpa [rexp_cexp_aux] using hf
    norm_cast at hf
  replace hFf : Integrable (𝓕 g) := by
    have h2π : 2 * π ≠ 0 := by simp
    have : Integrable (𝓕 (fun u ↦ rexp (-(σ * u)) • f (rexp (-u)))) := by
      simpa [mellin_eq_fourier, mul_div_cancel_right₀ _ h2π] using hFf.comp_mul_right' h2π
    simp_rw [neg_mul_eq_neg_mul] at this
    exact this
  replace hfx : ContinuousAt g (-Real.log x) := by
    refine ContinuousAt.fun_smul (by fun_prop) (ContinuousAt.comp ?_ (by fun_prop))
    simpa [Real.exp_log hx] using hfx
  calc
    mellinInv σ (mellin f) x
      = mellinInv σ (fun s ↦ 𝓕 g (s.im / (2 * π))) x := by
      simp [g, mellinInv, mellin_eq_fourier]
    _ = (x : ℂ) ^ (-σ : ℂ) • g (-Real.log x) := by
      rw [mellinInv_eq_fourierInv _ _ hx, ← hf.fourierInv_fourier_eq hFf hfx]

  have step1 := mellin_comp_rpow P.g (-s) (-1)
  simp_rw [abs_neg, abs_one, inv_one, one_smul, ofReal_neg, ofReal_one, div_neg, div_one, neg_neg,

  have step2 := mellin_cpow_smul (fun t ↦ P.g (1 / t)) (P.k - s) (-P.k)
  rw [← sub_eq_add_neg, sub_right_comm, sub_self, zero_sub, step1] at step2
  -- put in the constant `P.ε`
  have step3 := mellin_const_smul (fun t ↦ (t : ℂ) ^ (-P.k : ℂ) • P.g (1 / t)) (P.k - s) P.ε
  rw [step2] at step3
  rw [← step3]
  -- now the integrand matches `P.h_feq'` on `Ioi 0`, so we can apply `setIntegral_congr_fun`

  simp_rw [P.h_feq' t ht, ← mul_smul]
  -- some simple `cpow` arithmetic to finish
  rw [cpow_neg, ofReal_cpow (le_of_lt ht)]
  have : (t : ℂ) ^ (P.k : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by simpa [← ofReal_cpow ht.le] using (rpow_pos_of_pos ht _).ne'
  field_simp [P.hε]

## Lean formalization

`LandauIntegralTransfer.lean` proves the reusable continuous Taylor--Tonelli theorem for a
nonnegative random variable: analytic continuation of its complex MGF through a closed ball
forces every positive exponential moment strictly inside that ball.

`MobiusLaplaceLandauOscillation.lean` then formalizes the complete source specialization:

- unconditional sharp geometric estimate `||Phi(x)|| <= 1/x` and classical Mellin convergence;
- exact power-comparison Mellin identity and entire cutoff-tail transform;
- low-height quotient analyticity from `xi_ne_zero_of_abs_im_le_four`;
- positive density measure, translated MGF identity, and both Landau sign transfers;
- analytic reconstruction of `Gamma/zeta` across a half-plane with edge below `1/2`;
- collision with `xiDivisorSupport_infinite` after functional-equation reflection;
- arbitrary two-sided subcritical excursions and positive zeros below every `delta>0`.

All target modules compile with `lake env lean`; no `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `opaque`, or
`unsafe` declaration is introduced.  Remaining open endpoint is still exact exponent `1/2`.

## Frontier consequence

The half-power exponent is a genuine zero-edge oscillation barrier from below: every weaker power
normalization fails by unbounded positive and negative excursions.  Any viable proof of the open
upper bound must therefore control an intrinsically cofinal oscillatory source; eventual
positivity, monotonicity, finite sign charts, and subcritical absolute majorants are impossible.
The remaining open core is exactly sharp upper cancellation at exponent `1/2`, or equivalently
the already formalized Mellin continuation wall.

## Paper proof

On `w = σ + it`,
`|exp(w²)| = exp(σ²) exp(-t²)` and `|w| ≥ |σ|`; hence both
`exp(w²)/w` and `x⁻ʷexp(w²)/w` have explicit integrable Gaussian
majorants for `σ ≠ 0`. Between two positive abscissae, the integrand is
holomorphic and horizontal rectangle edges vanish like `exp(-T²)`, so the
vertical integrals agree.

For a contour crossing zero, write
`H(w) = x⁻ʷexp(w²)`. Since `H(0) = 1`,
`H(w)/w = 1/w + dslope H 0 w` away from zero; the divided difference is
entire. Its rectangle integral is zero. Direct real integration gives
`∫_{-T}^{T}(σ+it)⁻¹dt → π` for `σ>0` and `→ -π` for `σ<0`,
while both horizontal reciprocal integrals vanish. Thus positive minus
negative vertical integrals equal `2π`, and normalization by `1/(2π)`
gives the exact jump `1`.

## The `t`-integral — Halász's mean-value estimate for the series

`formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/Sieve/HalaszIntegralBound.lean` (9069 jobs, exit 0, axiom-clean).

  covering bound applies to it.
- `integral_norm_tsum_twistedSummand_le` — **the mean-value bound**:

  `∫_{-T}^{T} ‖∑_n f(n)n^{-σ-it}‖ dt ≤ damped·2T + trivial·(2T log z/π + 1)·2√(2π²δ²/logSqWeight z)`

Every constant is explicit and absolute; the only inputs are `|f| ≤ 1`, multiplicativity on coprime
arguments, and `σ > 1`. This is Halász's mean-value estimate for the object Perron inversion consumes.

# FZZ-P covariant reporter conservation rigidity

- **ID:** FZZ-P-HC8
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM / unique moving-reporter classification and selection no-go
- **Source:** HC6 exact flow + HC7 full coefficient-space action
- **Lean:** `GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.FZZCigarParityCovariantReporterConservationRigidity`
- **Statement:** A unique source-covariant moving Hermitian reporter exactly conserves unit diagonal
  energy, but it conserves the complete reflected mismatch and therefore cannot produce matching.

## Main theorem

For the HC6 stabilized flow, write

`e=exp(Pt)`, `k=(Q/R)(e-1)`

and

`q=k/e=(Q/R)(1-exp(-Pt))`.

The moving Hermitian reporter

`C_t=(q^2,q,0,1)`

satisfies, for every real time and state,

`H_(C_t)(Phi_t u)=H_(0,0,0,1)(u)`.

At coefficient level this reporter is unique: the pullback equations

`A'=0`, `B'=0`, `C'=0`, `d'=1`

hold exactly when `(a,b,c,d)=(q^2,q,0,1)`.

For every centered Mellin carrier and every time,

`H_(C_t)(Phi_t M(rho))=H_(C_t)(Phi_t M(reflect rho)) <-> Re rho=1/2`.

More strongly, the whole reflected reading difference is independent of time and equals the
initial unit-diagonal reflected defect.  Thus every off-wall carrier remains unmatched at every
time.  Universal covariant matching on all open-strip parity-Mellin modes at any chosen scale and
time is equivalent to RH.

## Paper proof

HC7 gives the pulled coefficients

`(e^2 a-2 e k b+k^2 d, e b-k d, e c, d)`.

Substitution of `(q^2,q,0,1)` with `q=k/e` reduces these to `(0,0,0,1)`, proving conservation.
Conversely, `d=1`; since `e>0`, `ec=0` forces `c=0`; then `eb-kd=0` forces `b=k/e=q`; finally the
first equation forces `a=q^2`.  This proves uniqueness without any zero or target input.

Apply conservation first to `M(rho)` and then to `M(reflect rho)`.  HC5's unit-diagonal detector
theorem yields the critical-line equivalence.  Subtracting the two identities proves exact defect
conservation.  Quantifying matching over source-defined parity-Mellin modes converts the moving
predicate to HC3's unit-diagonal matching predicate, already proved equivalent to RH.

## New route knowledge

- fixed all-time reporters fail, but a unique contragredient moving reporter exists;
- its coefficients are source-only and explicit at every real time;
- moving compensation removes HC6/HC7 cone escape at pullback level;
- conservation retains the detector but preserves every off-wall mismatch exactly;
- covariant transport is therefore kinematic, not dissipative or selective;
- universal divisor matching has unchanged RH proof burden;
- surviving FZZ-P dynamics must contain nonconservative interaction, nonlinear feedback,

From §218.1, unconditionally and with absolute convergence for `y > 0`,
```
Σ_{n≥1}a_F(n²)\,e^{−yn²} \;=\; ∫_0^1 θ(β)\,Θ_F(β,y)\,dβ ,\qquad
Θ_F(β,y) = Σ_m a_F(m)e(−mβ)e^{−ym} ,
```
`Θ_F` being the **damped linear twist**. By Mellin, a pole of `D_F(s) = Σ_n a_F(n²)n^{−s}` at `s = 1`
of order `κ` corresponds to `Σ_n a_F(n²)e^{−yn²} ∼ c\,y^{−1/2}(\log 1/y)^{κ−1}` as `y → 0^+`.

> **So (PSD₂) is the `y → 0` asymptotic of a pairing between the classical theta function and the damped

> linear twist** — exactly what Kaczorowski–Perelli supply in degree 2 (arXiv:1207.2312).

`G = L(s,χ)`, `d = 1`. Then `Σ_n a_G(n²)e^{−yn²} = Σ_nχ(n)²e^{−yn²}`, and:

/-
Exponent arithmetic of a bound for divisor sums against a `k`-th-root phase.

For `G_k(y) = Σ_{m≤y} d_k(m) e(k y^{1/k} m^{1/k})` the Mellin representation is
`G_k(y) = (1/2πi)∫ζ(s)^k M(s)ds` with `M(s) = k∫_1^V v^{ks-1}e(kXv)dv`, `X = V = y^{1/k}`.
Stationary phase gives `|M| ≍ √k · v₀^{(k-1)/2}/√X` at `v₀ = |t|/(2πX)`, supported on `|t| ≤ 2πXV`,
so the mass sits at `T = XV = y^{2/k}`.

Hölder against the fourth moment of `ζ` (exponents `4/k` and `4/(4-k)`, valid for `k < 4`, and by
continuity at `k = 4`) yields

    |G_k(y)| ≪ (∫_{|t|≍T}|ζ|^4)^{k/4} · (∫|M|^{q})^{1/q},   q = 4/(4-k),

and the two exponents combine to `1/2 + 1/k`.  The same computation with the sixth moment
(`m(3) ≤ 5/4`) covers `4 < k < 6` and gives `5/12 + (k+6)/(6k)`.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.MomentChordPivot

namespace HTGeometry

/-- Exponent delivered by Hölder against the fourth moment: `1/2 + 1/k`. -/
def fourthMomentPhaseExponent (k : ℚ) : ℚ := 1/2 + 1/k

@[simp] theorem fourthMomentPhaseExponent_three : fourthMomentPhaseExponent 3 = 5/6 := by
  unfold fourthMomentPhaseExponent; norm_num

@[simp] theorem fourthMomentPhaseExponent_four : fourthMomentPhaseExponent 4 = 3/4 := by
  unfold fourthMomentPhaseExponent; norm_num

/-- At `k = 2` the exponent is `1` — the method gives exactly nothing, as it must, since the
stationary-phase mass and the trivial bound coincide there. -/
@[simp] theorem fourthMomentPhaseExponent_two : fourthMomentPhaseExponent 2 = 1 := by
  unfold fourthMomentPhaseExponent; norm_num

/-- **Nontrivial exactly for `k > 2`.** -/
theorem fourthMomentPhaseExponent_lt_one {k : ℚ} (hk : 0 < k) :
    fourthMomentPhaseExponent k < 1 ↔ 2 < k := by
  unfold fourthMomentPhaseExponent
  constructor
  · intro h
    have : (1:ℚ)/k < 1/2 := by linarith
    rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ hk (by norm_num)] at this
    linarith
  · intro h
    have : (1:ℚ)/k < 1/2 := by
      rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ hk (by norm_num)]; linarith
    linarith

/-- The exponent decreases in `k`: higher divisor functions get better savings from the same
fourth-moment input. -/
theorem fourthMomentPhaseExponent_strictAnti {k l : ℚ} (hk : 0 < k) (hkl : k < l) :
    fourthMomentPhaseExponent l < fourthMomentPhaseExponent k := by
  unfold fourthMomentPhaseExponent
  have hl : (0:ℚ) < l := lt_trans hk hkl
  have : (1:ℚ)/l < 1/k := by rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ hl hk]; linarith
  linarith

/-- Exponent delivered by Hölder against the sixth moment with `m(3) ≤ 5/4`, valid for `4 < k < 6`. -/
def sixthMomentPhaseExponent (k : ℚ) : ℚ := 5/12 + (k + 6) / (6 * k)

@[simp] theorem sixthMomentPhaseExponent_five : sixthMomentPhaseExponent 5 = 47/60 := by
  unfold sixthMomentPhaseExponent; norm_num

/-- At `k = 4` the fourth-moment route is strictly better, so the crossover is above `4`. -/
theorem fourth_beats_sixth_at_four :
    fourthMomentPhaseExponent 4 < sixthMomentPhaseExponent 4 := by
  rw [fourthMomentPhaseExponent_four]
  unfold sixthMomentPhaseExponent; norm_num

/-- What the best known exponent pair gives for the same sum: `κ+λ ≤ 1 − kη` with Bourgain's
`κ+λ = 17/21`, i.e. `η ≤ 4/(21k)`. -/
def exponentPairPhaseExponent (k : ℚ) : ℚ := 1 - 4 / (21 * k)

/-- **The fourth-moment route beats the best exponent pair exactly for `k > 50/21 = 2.38…`.**  In
particular at every integer `k ≥ 3`.  (The two coincide at `k = 50/21`; below it the exponent pair is
better, but there the fourth-moment exponent is already close to trivial.) -/
theorem fourthMoment_beats_exponentPair {k : ℚ} (hk : 50/21 < k) :
    fourthMomentPhaseExponent k < exponentPairPhaseExponent k := by
  have hk0 : (0:ℚ) < k := by linarith
  unfold fourthMomentPhaseExponent exponentPairPhaseExponent
  rw [← sub_pos]
  have h1 : (1:ℚ) - 4/(21*k) - (1/2 + 1/k) = 1/2 - 25/(21*k) := by
    field_simp; ring
  rw [h1, sub_pos, div_lt_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by norm_num)]
  linarith

@[simp] theorem exponentPairPhaseExponent_three : exponentPairPhaseExponent 3 = 59/63 := by
  unfold exponentPairPhaseExponent; norm_num

end HTGeometry

`Gamma (s + 2*k) / n^(s+k)`.

After the second factorial normalization of a Borel transform, the first physical winding
`n = 1` therefore has coefficient

`b_k(s) = Gamma (s + 2*k) / (k!)^2`.

This file proves its exact consecutive growth law

`b_(k+1)(s) = R_k(s) b_k(s)`,

where

`R_k(s) = (s + 2*k) (s + 2*k + 1) / (k+1)^2`.

The functional-equation partner has a coefficient-faithful asymmetry at every Borel grade:

`R_k(s) - R_k(1-s) = 4 (2*k+1) (s-1/2) / (k+1)^2`.

Thus equality of the real partner growth rates is exactly critical-line placement, already at
one grade.  Requiring this balance at every actual Xi zero is equivalent to RH.

no positive diagonal change of recoil-grade metric can make the two edges adjoints away from the
critical line.  This eliminates rate-level KMS and arbitrary metric reweighting as ways to hide

/-!
# The Riesz mean as a logarithmic average of partial sums

The second-order Riesz mean carries the weight `log(N/n)`.  Telescoping that weight,

```text
log N - log n = ∑_{m=n}^{N-1} ( log(m+1) - log m ) ,
```

and exchanging the two finite sums turns the weighted sum of coefficients into a weighted sum of
*partial* sums:

```text
∑_{n < N} aₙ ( log N - log(n+1) ) = ∑_{m < N} ( log(m+1) - log m ) · ∑_{n < m} aₙ .
```

The weights are nonnegative and add up to `log N`, so a uniform bound on the partial sums transfers
to the Riesz mean with the factor `log N`.  This is the discrete half of the Riesz-mean method,
requiring no contour integral; the analytic half is the kernel `1/w²` and its Mellin pair.
-/

noncomputable section

open Finset

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

/-- The logarithmic increments telescope to `log N`. -/
theorem sum_log_increment (N : ℕ) :
    ∑ m ∈ Finset.range N, (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) = Real.log (N : ℝ) := by
  have h : ∑ m ∈ Finset.range N, (Real.log ((m : ℕ) + 1 : ℕ) - Real.log ((m : ℕ) : ℕ))
      = Real.log ((N : ℕ) : ℝ) - Real.log ((0 : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    Finset.sum_range_sub (fun m : ℕ => Real.log ((m : ℕ) : ℝ)) N
  simpa using h

/-- Each logarithmic increment is nonnegative. -/
theorem log_increment_nonneg (m : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with hm | hm
  · subst hm
    simp
  · have hm0 : (0 : ℝ) < (m : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hm
    have : Real.log (m : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) :=
      Real.log_le_log hm0 (by linarith)
    linarith

/-- **The Riesz mean is a logarithmic average of the partial sums.** -/
theorem rieszLogSum_eq_sum_partialSum (a : ℕ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) :
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
      = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range N,
          ((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℂ))
            * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n) := by
  induction N with
  | zero => simp
  | succ N ih =>
    have hsplit : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1),
          a n * ((Real.log ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
        = (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N,
            a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ)))
          + ((Real.log ((N : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ))
            * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ]
      have hlast : a N * ((Real.log ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
          - (Real.log ((N : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ)) = 0 := by
        have hcast : ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
        rw [hcast]
        ring
      have hterm : ∀ n ∈ Finset.range N,
          a n * ((Real.log ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
            = a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))
              + ((Real.log ((N : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ)) * a n := by
        intro n _
        have hcast : ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
        rw [hcast]
        ring
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
      have hcast : ((N + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
      rw [hcast] at hlast ⊢
      rw [hlast, add_zero]
    rw [hsplit, ih, Finset.sum_range_succ]

/-- **A uniform bound on the partial sums bounds the Riesz mean by `log N` times that bound.** -/
theorem norm_rieszLogSum_le {a : ℕ → ℂ} {B : ℝ} {N : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ m ∈ Finset.range N, ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n‖ ≤ B) :
    ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, a n * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℂ) - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ))‖
      ≤ B * Real.log (N : ℝ) := by
  rw [rieszLogSum_eq_sum_partialSum]
  refine le_trans (norm_sum_le _ _) ?_
  have hterm : ∀ m ∈ Finset.range N,
      ‖((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℂ))
        * (∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n)‖
        ≤ B * (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) := by
    intro m hm
    have hw : ((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) : ℂ) - (Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℂ))
        = ((Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
      push_cast
      ring
    rw [hw, norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_nonneg (log_increment_nonneg m)]
    calc (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) * ‖∑ n ∈ Finset.range m, a n‖
        ≤ (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) * B :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h m hm) (log_increment_nonneg m)
      _ = B * (Real.log ((m : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log (m : ℝ)) := by ring
  refine le_trans (Finset.sum_le_sum hterm) ?_
  rw [← Finset.mul_sum, sum_log_increment]

end GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

/-!
# A quantitative Nyman–Beurling criterion, with explicit modulus

The three ingredients left open by the boundary/interior dichotomy assemble.

**(a) The space.**  Every Báez-Duarte generator is supported in `(0,1]`: for `t ≥ 1` both `1/t < 1`
and `θ/t < 1`, so `ρ_θ(t) = {θ/t} - θ{1/t} = θ/t - θ/t = 0`.  The target `1_{(0,1]}` is likewise
supported there.  The Mellin transform `f ↦ ∫₀¹ f(t)t^{-s}dt` therefore converges for `Re s < ½` and
maps `L²((0,1],dt)` unitarily onto the Hardy space `H²` of the half-plane `Re s < ½`, with the
Plancherel normalization

```text
‖f‖² = (1/2π) ∫_ℝ |f̂(½+iu)|² du ,
```

as the target itself confirms: `1̂(s) = 1/(1-s)`, whose boundary modulus squared integrates to `2π`,
matching `‖1_{(0,1]}‖² = 1`.

**(b) The vanishing constraint.**  The transform of a generator is `ζ(s)(n^{-s} - 1/n)/s`, so every
finite combination has transform `ζ(s)P(s)/s` with `P` entire.  At a zero `ρ` of `ζ` with `ρ ≠ 0`
this vanishes, and vanishing is preserved under `L²` limits because point evaluation in `H²` is
continuous.  The target does not vanish there: `1̂(ρ) = 1/(1-ρ) ≠ 0`.

**(c) The cost.**  With this normalization the diagonal kernel of `H²` of a half-plane is
`K(w,w) = 1/(2σ)`, `σ` the distance from `w` to the boundary line.  (The preceding module used the
unnormalized convention, where the constant is `1/(4πσ)`; the dichotomy is the same and only the
constant differs.)  The exact vanishing cost therefore gives, for a zero `ρ = β + iγ` of `ζ` with
`β < ½`,

```text
lim_N d_N  ≥  |1̂(ρ)| / √K(ρ,ρ)  =  √(1 - 2β) / |1 - ρ| .
```

By the functional equation the Riemann hypothesis fails exactly when such a `ρ` exists, so

> **If the Riemann hypothesis fails, the Báez-Duarte distances are bounded below by the explicit
> constant `√(1-2β)/|1-ρ|` for every zero `ρ` with `Re ρ < ½`.**

This is the quantitative form of the easy direction of the Nyman–Beurling criterion: not merely
`d_N ↛ 0`, but a modulus in the deviation.

**Universal height degradation.**  The constant is at most `1/|γ|`, since `√(1-2β) ≤ 1` and
`|1-ρ| ≥ |γ|`.  So a counterexample high up produces only a tiny floor, and combining the criterion
with numerical verification to height `X` would require the complementary analytic bound
`d_N ≤ 1/X` — with `d_N² ≍ 1/log N` that means `N ≥ exp(X²)`.  The same degradation appeared in the
flow lane, where verification to height `X` bounds `Λ` only by `π²/(2 log²X)`.  It is not an artefact
of either method:

> **Every quantified lane loses strength at a putative counterexample polynomially or exponentially
> in its height.  Numerical verification and analytic estimate never meet unless the analytic
> estimate is itself as strong as the verification height.**

That is the unified reason the "verify below, estimate above" architecture stalls, and it applies to
the Nyman–Beurling lane exactly as it does to the de Bruijn–Newman lane.

This file formalizes the kernel with the correct normalization, the explicit floor, and the height
degradation.
-/

open Real

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- The diagonal reproducing kernel of `H²` of a half-plane in the Plancherel normalization
`‖F‖² = (1/2π)∫|F|²`. -/
def nymanBeurlingHardyKernel (sigma : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 / (2 * sigma)

/-- **The explicit floor.**  The cost of vanishing at a point at distance `σ` from the boundary, for
a target of modulus `m` there, is `m·√(2σ)`. -/
def nbFloor (m sigma : ℝ) : ℝ := m * Real.sqrt (2 * sigma)

/-- The floor is the target modulus divided by the square root of the diagonal kernel. -/
theorem nbFloor_eq {m sigma : ℝ} (hs : 0 < sigma) :
    nbFloor m sigma = m / Real.sqrt (nymanBeurlingHardyKernel sigma) := by
  unfold nbFloor nymanBeurlingHardyKernel
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 2 * sigma := by positivity
  rw [one_div, Real.sqrt_inv, div_inv_eq_mul]

/-- **Positivity.**  A zero strictly off the critical line gives a strictly positive floor. -/
theorem nbFloor_pos {m sigma : ℝ} (hm : 0 < m) (hs : 0 < sigma) : 0 < nbFloor m sigma := by
  unfold nbFloor
  have : 0 < Real.sqrt (2 * sigma) := Real.sqrt_pos.mpr (by positivity)
  positivity

/-- **The floor in terms of the zero.**  With `σ = ½ - β` and `m = 1/|1-ρ|`, the floor is
`√(1-2β)/|1-ρ|`. -/
theorem nbFloor_of_zero (beta r : ℝ) :
    nbFloor (1 / r) (1 / 2 - beta) = Real.sqrt (1 - 2 * beta) / r := by
  unfold nbFloor
  have h2 : 2 * (1 / 2 - beta) = 1 - 2 * beta := by ring
  rw [h2, one_div, inv_mul_eq_div]

/-- **Height degradation.**  Since `√(1-2β) ≤ 1` for `β ≥ 0` and `|1-ρ| ≥ |γ|`, the floor is at most
`1/|γ|`: a counterexample high up gives only a tiny floor. -/
theorem nbFloor_le_inv_height {beta r g : ℝ} (hb0 : 0 ≤ beta)
    (hg : 0 < g) (hr : g ≤ r) :
    Real.sqrt (1 - 2 * beta) / r ≤ 1 / g := by
  have hrpos : 0 < r := lt_of_lt_of_le hg hr
  have hle : Real.sqrt (1 - 2 * beta) ≤ 1 := by
    have h1 : 1 - 2 * beta ≤ 1 := by linarith

The source puncture coordinate of an actual inverse-Gamma sheet is exactly the target coordinate

/-- Pole-centered, factorially normalized actual inverse-Gamma sheet over the source puncture. -/

  (gammaExteriorInverseBranch n (gammaPunctureExteriorLift z) + (n : ℂ)) /
    reciprocalGammaFactorialScale n

branch at the positive Laurent coordinate. -/

  have hscale : reciprocalGammaFactorialScale n ≠ 0 := by
    exact div_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero _ (by norm_num))
      (by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_ne_zero n)
  rw [gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet, gammaExteriorInverseBranch,
    ← gammaPunctureCoordinate_eq_neg_inv_exteriorLift]
  field_simp [hscale]
  ring

/-- **Puncture--moving-base chart law.**  The intrinsic moving-base coordinate is the exact
Möbius transform of the pole-normalized actual Gamma sheet. -/
theorem gammaMovingBaseTransition_puncture_eq_mobius_normalizedSheet
    (n : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    gammaMovingBaseTransition n (gammaPunctureCoordinate z) =
      mobiusTangentGerm (gammaMovingBaseShell n)
        (gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet n z) := by
  rw [gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet_eq_branch]
  rfl

/-- The normalized actual sheet is invariant under the puncture deck translation. -/
theorem gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet_shift (n : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet n
        (z + 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I) =
      gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet n z := by
  rw [gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet, gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet,
    gammaExteriorInverseBranch_puncture_shift]

/-- The transported moving-base coordinate is also puncture-deck invariant. -/
theorem gammaMovingBaseTransition_puncture_shift (n : ℕ) (z : ℂ) :
    gammaMovingBaseTransition n
        (gammaPunctureCoordinate
          (z + 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)) =
      gammaMovingBaseTransition n (gammaPunctureCoordinate z) := by
  rw [gammaPunctureCoordinate_shift]

/-- **Actual-sheet capacity law.**  On the common puncture collar, the moving-base tangent metric
of the genuine Gamma sheet is uniformly congruent to its pole-normalized tangent metric, with
absolute constants independent of pole depth. -/
theorem gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet_capacity_congruent
    {n : ℕ} (hn : gammaCommonInverseCollar.threshold ≤ n)
    {z v : ℂ}
    (hz : gammaPunctureCoordinate z ∈ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℂ) (1 / 4))

        16 * ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
  rw [gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet_eq_branch]
  exact gammaMovingBaseTransition_capacity_congruent hn hz hshell

/-- The actual-sheet tangent comparison is asymptotically isometric at every fixed point of the
common puncture collar. -/
theorem tendsto_gammaPunctureNormalizedSheet_tangentFactor_one
    {z : ℂ}
    (hz : gammaPunctureCoordinate z ∈ Metric.closedBall (0 : ℂ) (1 / 4)) :
    Tendsto

/-!
# The irreversible clock on the dimension-zero Gamma horizon

The linearly receding inverse-Gamma constraint is forward invariant under `Gamma`.  In the Baire
coordinates of `GammaDimensionZeroHorizon`, the induced clock is

`tau(omega)(k) = omega(k + 1) + 1`.

Thus `Gamma` deletes one inverse-sheet label and records the elapsed depth in every surviving
label.  This is an exact consequence of the static inverse-history constraint, not an assumed
flow.  Its age filtration is strictly decreasing and has empty infinite-age core; consequently
the constrained horizon has no periodic Gamma histories.  All statements are for the actual
Euler Gamma function.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

open Complex Filter Function Set Topology

noncomputable section

/-- The clock induced on Baire histories by the linearly receding Gamma constraint. -/
def gammaHorizonClock (omega : Nat -> Nat) : Nat -> Nat :=
  fun k => omega (k + 1) + 1

@[simp]
theorem gammaHorizonClock_apply (omega : Nat -> Nat) (k : Nat) :
    gammaHorizonClock omega k = omega (k + 1) + 1 := rfl

/-- Finite inverse words agree whenever their actual pole labels agree. -/
theorem gammaCodePrefix_eq_of_labels
    {N M omega nu : Nat -> Nat} {d : Nat}
    (hlabel : ∀ k, k < d -> gammaCodeLabel N omega k = gammaCodeLabel M nu k)
    (y : Complex) :
    gammaCodePrefix N omega d y = gammaCodePrefix M nu d y := by
  induction d generalizing N M omega nu with
  | zero => simp
  | succ d ih =>
      rw [gammaCodePrefix_succ, gammaCodePrefix_succ]
      congr 1
      · exact hlabel 0 (by omega)
      · apply ih
        intro k hk
        simpa [gammaCodeLabel, gammaCodeShift] using hlabel (k + 1) (by omega)

/-- The complex horizon point depends only on the sequence of actual pole labels, not on how a
label is split into a schedule and an offset word. -/
theorem gammaBaireCode_eq_of_labels
    {N M omega nu : Nat -> Nat}
    (hlabel : ∀ k, gammaCodeLabel N omega k = gammaCodeLabel M nu k) :
    gammaBaireCode N omega = gammaBaireCode M nu := by
  exact congrArg (fun u : Nat -> Complex => limUnder Filter.atTop u) (by
    funext d
    exact gammaCodePrefix_eq_of_labels (fun k _hk => hlabel k) gammaCodeBase)

theorem gammaThinSchedule_clock_label (omega : Nat -> Nat) (k : Nat) :
    gammaCodeLabel gammaThinSchedule (gammaHorizonClock omega) k =
      gammaCodeLabel (gammaCodeShift gammaThinSchedule) (gammaCodeShift omega) k := by
  simp [gammaCodeLabel, gammaThinSchedule, gammaHorizonClock, gammaCodeShift]
  omega

/-- **Exact emergent-clock law.**  On the dimension-zero horizon, actual Euler Gamma is the
delete-and-age clock `omega |-> (omega(k+1)+1)_k`. -/
theorem Gamma_gammaConstrainedHorizon_code (omega : Nat -> Nat) :
    Complex.Gamma (gammaBaireCode gammaThinSchedule omega) =
      gammaBaireCode gammaThinSchedule (gammaHorizonClock omega) := by
  calc
    Complex.Gamma (gammaBaireCode gammaThinSchedule omega) =
        gammaBaireCode (gammaCodeShift gammaThinSchedule) (gammaCodeShift omega) :=
      Gamma_gammaBaireCode gammaThinSchedule_late
    _ = gammaBaireCode gammaThinSchedule (gammaHorizonClock omega) :=
      (gammaBaireCode_eq_of_labels (gammaThinSchedule_clock_label omega)).symm

/-- The constrained horizon is forward invariant under the actual Gamma function. -/
theorem Gamma_mapsTo_gammaConstrainedHorizon :
    MapsTo Complex.Gamma gammaConstrainedHorizon gammaConstrainedHorizon := by
  rintro _ ⟨omega, rfl⟩
  exact ⟨gammaHorizonClock omega, (Gamma_gammaConstrainedHorizon_code omega).symm⟩

/-- The actual Gamma self-map of the constrained horizon. -/
def gammaConstrainedHorizonMap : gammaConstrainedHorizon -> gammaConstrainedHorizon :=
  fun z => ⟨Complex.Gamma z, Gamma_mapsTo_gammaConstrainedHorizon z.2⟩

/-- The Baire homeomorphism exactly intertwines the emergent clock with restricted Gamma. -/
theorem gammaConstrainedHorizonHomeomorph_intertwines (omega : Nat -> Nat) :
    gammaConstrainedHorizonHomeomorph (gammaHorizonClock omega) =
      gammaConstrainedHorizonMap (gammaConstrainedHorizonHomeomorph omega) := by
  apply Subtype.ext
  exact (Gamma_gammaConstrainedHorizon_code omega).symm

@[simp]
theorem gammaHorizonClock_iterate_apply (omega : Nat -> Nat) (d k : Nat) :
    (gammaHorizonClock^[d]) omega k = omega (k + d) + d := by
  induction d generalizing k with
  | zero => simp
  | succ d ih =>
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']
      simp only [gammaHorizonClock_apply, ih]
      rw [show k + 1 + d = k + (d + 1) by omega]
      omega

/-- Every finite Gamma iterate reads the tail and adds the elapsed age to all surviving labels. -/
theorem Gamma_iterate_gammaConstrainedHorizon_code (omega : Nat -> Nat) (d : Nat) :
    (Complex.Gamma^[d]) (gammaBaireCode gammaThinSchedule omega) =
      gammaBaireCode gammaThinSchedule ((gammaHorizonClock^[d]) omega) := by
  induction d with
  | zero => simp
  | succ d ih =>

# Finite Signed Even Frequency Atoms Are Not Markov

- **ID:** finite-signed-even-frequency-atoms-not-markov
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / source-transfer guardrail
- **Grade:** BRIDGE / guardrail. Door-2 reduces the proof to finite
  exponential-sum dominance, so this is not a native theorem. Its use is to
  exclude a false source-transfer shape.
- **Source:** `positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md`;
  `source-selector-repair-obligation-ledger.md`;
  `seam-log-markov-pick-rh-equivalence.md`
- **Statement:** A nonzero finite signed sum of real FE-even exponential
  frequency germs cannot produce a Markov/Stieltjes moment sequence in the
  seam-square coordinate. Its shifted moments are negative on infinitely many
  indices.

## Setup

Let `n>=1`, and let

`0 < lambda_1 < ... < lambda_n`

and let `c_1,...,c_n` be real coefficients with `c_n != 0`. Equal frequencies
are first combined, so the displayed top coefficient is nonzero. Define

`L(z)=sum_{j=1}^n c_j (cosh(lambda_j sqrt(z))-1)`.

For `k>=1`, define the shifted seam moments

`T_k=-2k(-1)^k [z^k]L(z)`.

Set `x_j=lambda_j^2`.

## Theorem

If the signed frequency sum is nonzero, then there are infinitely many `k` for
which

`T_k < 0`.

Consequently `(T_k)_{k>=1}` is not the moment sequence of a positive Borel
measure on `R_+`. In particular, the finite signed real FE-even frequency atom
span intersects the Markov/Stieltjes target only at zero.

## Proof

The coefficient calculation gives

`[z^k]L(z)=sum_{j=1}^n c_j lambda_j^(2k)/(2k)!`

and hence

`T_k = (-1)^(k+1) (sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j^k)/(2k-1)!`.

Let

`S_k=sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j^k`.

Since `0 < x_1 < ... < x_n`,

`S_k / x_n^k = c_n + sum_{j<n} c_j (x_j/x_n)^k -> c_n`.

Thus, for all sufficiently large `k`, `S_k` has the sign of `c_n`.

If `c_n>0`, then for every sufficiently large even `k`,

`T_k = - S_k/(2k-1)! < 0`.

If `c_n<0`, then for every sufficiently large odd `k`,

`T_k = S_k/(2k-1)! < 0`.

In either case infinitely many shifted moments are negative. Since every moment
of a positive measure on `R_+` is nonnegative, no positive Markov/Stieltjes
representation exists.

## Consequence For Signed Counterterm Routes

`positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md` ruled out positive summation over
FE-even real frequencies. This theorem rules out the finite signed atomic
escape as well. A signed correction made from finitely many real FE-even
frequency atoms cannot repair the Markov target; the dominant frequency forces
tail sign oscillation.

Therefore a completed source proof cannot be a finite signed real-frequency
counterterm patched onto the positive cone. Any viable signed correction must
be genuinely outside this finite atom class: an infinite/nonlocal source object,
an archimedean-prime interaction, a multiplicative correlation identity, or a
closed boundary/index construction.

## Boundary

This theorem does not rule out infinite signed distributions with no largest
frequency, complex or imaginary frequencies, non-frequency source terms, or the
completed explicit formula. It only closes the finite real atom model.

## Theatre Test

For any proposed signed counterterm proof of seam-log Markov positivity:

1. Does the proof reduce the completed correction to finitely many real FE-even
   frequency atoms?
2. If yes, combine equal frequencies and inspect the top nonzero frequency.
3. The top frequency fixes the sign of `S_k` for large `k`, so `T_k` is negative
   on one tail parity.
4. Which source mechanism prevents that dominance argument from applying?

## Novelty Status

The proof is elementary finite exponential-sum dominance. The significant part
is the route audit: signed finite atom corrections are not the missing
completed interaction.

# Chronological chord capacity: computational leads

Exploratory numerical work, 2026-09-05. Results are not proof certificates. Scripts ran on the authorized Runpod (`157.157.221.29:27094`, directory `/root/chronological-chord-capacity`), with 24 Python workers and one BLAS/OpenMP thread per worker. Environment: 32 available CPUs, NumPy 1.24.4, SciPy 1.10.1. Source and result JSON files are retained here.

## Question and method

For a pairing D of ordered endpoints, put `P_D(d)=∏_(i,j in D) Σ_(i≤k<j) d_k`, with variation budget `Σ|d_k|=1`.

`search.py` tested all 121 nonzero ternary coefficient vectors up to overall sign in the five-dimensional noncrossing basis on six endpoints. Each of 32 seeds sampled 72,000 positive and 72,000 signed Dirichlet increment vectors (concentration 0.3). Twelve coefficient vectors with the strongest apparent signed advantage received constrained SLSQP refinement, with analytic gradients, all 16 sign patterns modulo overall sign, and both objective signs. Output: `results.json`.

`basis_probe.py` tested the stronger conjecture `Σ_D |P_D(d)|/cap(D) ≤ 1`, for all noncrossing pairings on 4–12 endpoints. Individual-diagram capacities were supplied by a recursive interval-product formula using rational arithmetic; that implementation is part of the exploratory model, not a formal certificate. For each chord count, six seeds and both sign classes used 2,500 Dirichlet samples and SLSQP refinement from the 12 strongest samples. Output: `basis-results.json`.

## Outcomes

The first experiment found no resolved advantage from signed probe motion. This finite search establishes no equality theorem, and the full signed-versus-monotone question remains open.

The normalized-basis conjecture failed decisively from three chords onward. Best numerical values, rounded:

| Chords | Observed maximum |
|---|---:|
| 2 | 1.000000 |
| 3 | 1.132006 |
| 4 | 1.410792 |
| 5 | 1.896740 |
| 6 | 2.690254 |

These are local numerical optima, not certified global maxima. Signed sampling did not improve the best monotone value at reported precision. Small errors above 1 in degree two are floating-point effects.

## Exact mathematical consequence

The three-chord result suggested the two-term combination `27D+R`, where `D=(01)(23)(45)` and `R=(05)(14)(23)`. At gaps `(1/3,0,1/3,0,1/3)`, cost is exactly 1 and response exactly `10/9`, disproving the proposed bound without numerical inputs.

Independent symbolic reasoning then gave the global optimum: `q=(50-√313)/81` and `K=27q(1-q)²/4+q²`. Gaps `((1-q)/2,0,q,0,(1-q)/2)` attain K. Triangle inequalities, endpoint AM–GM, and a factored cubic optimality gap prove the upper bound for every signed gap vector. This exact argument is checked in `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/HTGeometry/ChronologicalTensor/SixPoint.lean`; no JSON data or optimizer output enters Lean.

Further reasoning resolved the existence of signed advantage outside the first experiment's ternary coefficient class: `27D-R` has monotone capacity exactly 1, while gaps `(1/3,0,-1/3,0,1/3)` give `-28/27`. This is checked independently in `ChronologicalTensor/Reversal.lean`. It is not an output of either search.

Useful next questions concern composition across independent blocks and how nesting suppresses reversal-sensitive response. The degree 4–6 numerical values remain leads only.

# Signed prime recursion and changing arithmetic alignment

**Status:** two empirical hunches falsified; exact signed cofactor transport and a divisor information audit formalized. No new all-scale cancellation bound and no RH proof. Numerical results are exploratory, despite this folder's pipeline location.

Positivity is suspended as the proposed producer in this investigation. This is a research constraint, not a theorem that all positive or spectral methods fail. Corpus starting points, frozen predictions, controls, and adaptive decisions are in [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md).

## What the algebraic audit establishes

The actual observable is exactly

`R(N)=-sum(n<=N) lambda(n) w(n) - N sum(n<=N) lambda(n)/n`,

where `w(n)=sum(p prime dividing n) log p` counts each distinct prime divisor once. Expanding theta and reindexing the finite product region proves this: complete multiplicativity and the prime value -1 give `lambda(m)=-lambda(pm)`.

`LiouvillePrimeErrorDivisorAudit.lean` proves both the theta-pairing collapse and the full error identity, unconditionally and without computational premises. Scratch/direct checks and the named leaf build pass; both axiom audits contain only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The alignment observable therefore re-expresses weighted Liouville cancellation; it does not supply a second independent arithmetic constraint. A representation may still expose a useful estimate, but that estimate has not been found.

The cyclic-shift controls break complete multiplicativity. Their ranks discriminate from the chosen coarse-data controls, but cannot establish a mechanism beyond the multiplicative identity they destroy. The generic signed dilation theorem also holds for every ratio kernel, so that theorem alone does not distinguish the literal counting-error kernel. **Further alignment scans are paused.** A new experimental target must state a source-specific property or estimate, distinguish it from these identities, and specify controls that retain the properties it claims to use.

## What changed our understanding

The literal arithmetic does not consistently make the measured prime-counting error smaller. Relative to interventions preserving every dyadic cofactor block's sign count and signed sum, it can strongly suppress or strongly amplify the same error pairing. The reversal involves many cofactor scales and survives removing the smallest cofactors. An apparent doubling law mostly extends to other primes, but has decisive failures.

These observations reject a fixed direction of improvement for this observable. They do not yet identify a replacement asymptotic law. The exact residue specifies what a signed dilation argument must control instead of assuming reversal.

## Experiment 1: keep both discarded remainders

For a completely multiplicative sign function f and S(N)=sum(n<=N) f(n), the corpus's exact log recursion gives

`S(N) log N = P(N) + Elog(N) + Epp(N)`,

where P is the signed prime sum, Elog is the log-weight replacement error, and Epp is the complete contribution from higher prime powers. The existing general bounds on the two errors are O(N), inadequate for an RH producer.

At all **37** literal Liouville cutoffs from 4096 through 2097152, Elog and Epp have the same sign. At the last cutoff their values divided by sqrt(N) are approximately **-1.34944** and **-2.75630**. Their addition provides no saving. Four of seven random completely multiplicative controls also reinforce at every tested cutoff; the other three sometimes cancel. Thus the two discarded errors do not exhibit a distinctive hidden cancellation in this sample. See `results.json`.

# Perfect-pairing enclosure depth: numerical leads

**Outcome:** no validated numerical counterexample was found to depth-one stabilization in degrees three or four, or to depth-two stabilization in degree four. This finite search proves none of those universal statements. The known cubic reversal form has independently proved exact depth one; other coefficient combinations remain open.

## Question and method

For each noncrossing perfect pairing D on 2d ordered endpoints, form its gap polynomial `P_D=∏_(i,j∈D) Σ_(i≤q<j) g_q`. These give 5 generators in degree three and 14 in degree four. We searched coefficient combinations P for a signed variation-one probe with `|S^k P(g)|` greater than the monotone capacity, where S is total displacement.

The search ran on the authorized Runpod, in `/root/chronological-chord-capacity`, using 24 independent worker processes. Degree/depth pairs were (3,1), (4,1), and (4,2), with eight deterministic seeds each. BLAS/OpenMP environment variables were set to one thread before importing NumPy. SciPy 1.10.1 and NumPy 1.24.4 were used. The additional HiGHS `threads` option emitted `Unknown solver options: threads`; do not interpret the JSON's `library_threads` field as a measured backend thread count. The environment caps and 24-process pool are explicit in the source. The warning filter was broadened after the run to suppress this repeated diagnostic; numerical code is unchanged.

For each seed:

- A simplex grid plus 800 random monotone probes supplied 1,801 initial constraints in degree three or 2,516 in degree four.
- Linear programming selected coefficients against 40 signed target probes. Columns were scaled by their sampled maxima for conditioning.
- The best three candidates underwent at most ten rounds of monotone constraint exchange and optimization inside the signed probe's orthant, using analytic gradients and SLSQP.
- A first normalization check used 20,000 fresh monotone probes and local optimization.
- A separate validation used another 30,000 monotone probes per candidate, plus both the previously found monotone witness and the absolute value of the purported signed witness as optimization starts.

All 24 jobs completed. Three individual LP calls failed and were handled without treating their outputs as candidates. The search and validation are heuristic global searches; both can miss optima.

The last excess is floating-point scale. There is no robust violation in these results.

The initial degree-four, depth-two run at seed 6 reported a ratio of about 1.001605. Its signed probe was approximately `(0.2197901333,0,0,0.4505246355,0,0.3296852312,0)`, with only roundoff-sized negative entries. This is already a monotone probe. The apparent violation therefore exposed a missed monotone maximum. Including that probe in the monotone search removed the apparent excess. Future searches must always include the absolute signed candidate in monotone normalization, and should inspect negative mass before interpreting a ratio above one.

The LP/optimization loop frequently converged to monotone maximizers and positive-coefficient forms. This is a search limitation, not evidence that all signed coefficient combinations are controlled. A useful next step is a symbolic convex-hull or straightening argument for the five-generator cubic space, or a search deliberately constrained to retain nonzero reversal mass.

For a real completely multiplicative sign function f, put S(N)=sum(n<=N) f(n), and define

- Elog(N)=sum(n<=N) f(n) log(N/n);
- Eeven(N)=sum(p^k<=N, k>=2 even) log(p) f(p)^k S(floor(N/p^k));

/-!
# Continuous heat refinement of the sharp degree-four certificate

The degree-four witness can be retained through positive heat time instead of
being collapsed immediately at scale zero.  For a moment model `M`, define

`W_M(u) = sum_i w_i p(x_i)^2 exp(-u x_i^2)`,

where `p(x)=1-(7/4)x+(2/3)x^2` is the sharp quadratic witness.  Lean proves
that `W_M(u)` is exactly a fixed signed linear combination of the five
simultaneous heat moments of orders zero through four.

For every nonnegative heat scale, `1-2 W_M(u)` lies between the static
`13/18` certificate and the exact model certificate.  It is monotone in heat
time and converges to the exact certificate as `u` tends to infinity.  Thus
the continuous carrier really is an information-preserving refinement.

However, the explicit sharp three-atom model has `W_M(u)=5/36` at every
nonnegative scale: its two nonzero atoms are roots of `p`.  Consequently this
entire witness-damped heat family remains stuck at `13/18` on the adversarial
model.  Beating that ceiling requires an observable not annihilated by those
two root channels.  This is an abstract method-ceiling theorem, not an eta or
zeta-zero result.
-/

open Finset Filter Topology
open scoped BigOperators Classical

namespace RiemannGaussian

noncomputable section

/-! ## The witness-weighted heat carrier -/

/-- The quadratic-witness mass retained at heat scale `u`. -/
def DegreeFourMomentModel.witnessHeat
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (M : DegreeFourMomentModel ι) (u : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, M.weight i * degreeFourMomentWitness (M.node i) ^ 2 *
    Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)

/-- The corresponding scale-dependent lower certificate. -/
def DegreeFourMomentModel.heatCertificate
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (M : DegreeFourMomentModel ι) (u : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  1 - 2 * M.witnessHeat u

/-- The witness heat is a fixed signed linear combination of the five
simultaneous heat moments.  No moment order or heat scale is discarded. -/
theorem DegreeFourMomentModel.witnessHeat_eq_heatMomentCombination
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (M : DegreeFourMomentModel ι) (u : ℝ) :
    M.witnessHeat u =
      M.heatMoment 0 u - (7 / 2 : ℝ) * M.heatMoment 1 u +
        (211 / 48 : ℝ) * M.heatMoment 2 u -
        (7 / 3 : ℝ) * M.heatMoment 3 u +
        (4 / 9 : ℝ) * M.heatMoment 4 u := by
  unfold DegreeFourMomentModel.witnessHeat
    DegreeFourMomentModel.heatMoment
  calc
    ∑ i, M.weight i * degreeFourMomentWitness (M.node i) ^ 2 *
        Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2) =
      ∑ i, (M.weight i * Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2) -
        (7 / 2 : ℝ) *
          (M.weight i * M.node i * Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) +
        (211 / 48 : ℝ) *
          (M.weight i * M.node i ^ 2 * Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) -
        (7 / 3 : ℝ) *
          (M.weight i * M.node i ^ 3 * Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) +
        (4 / 9 : ℝ) *
          (M.weight i * M.node i ^ 4 * Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2))) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro i _hi
      unfold degreeFourMomentWitness
      ring
    _ =
      (∑ i, M.weight i * Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) -
        (7 / 2 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i * Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) +
        (211 / 48 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 2 *
            Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) -
        (7 / 3 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 3 *
            Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) +
        (4 / 9 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 4 *
            Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) := by
      simp only [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_sub_distrib,
        Finset.mul_sum]
    _ =
      (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 0 *
          Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) -
        (7 / 2 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 1 *
            Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) +
        (211 / 48 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 2 *
            Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) -
        (7 / 3 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 3 *
            Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) +
        (4 / 9 : ℝ) *
          (∑ i, M.weight i * M.node i ^ 4 *
            Real.exp (-u * M.node i ^ 2)) := by simp

/-- At zero heat scale, the witness carrier is exactly `5/36`. -/
@[simp] theorem DegreeFourMomentModel.witnessHeat_zero
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (M : DegreeFourMomentModel ι) :
    M.witnessHeat 0 = (5 : ℝ) / 36 := by
  unfold DegreeFourMomentModel.witnessHeat
  simpa using M.sum_weight_mul_witness_sq_eq

/-- The witness heat is nonnegative at every real scale. -/
theorem DegreeFourMomentModel.witnessHeat_nonneg
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (M : DegreeFourMomentModel ι) (u : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ M.witnessHeat u := by
  unfold DegreeFourMomentModel.witnessHeat
  apply Finset.sum_nonneg
  intro i _hi
  exact mul_nonneg
    (mul_nonneg (M.weight_nonneg i)
      (sq_nonneg (degreeFourMomentWitness (M.node i))))
    (Real.exp_pos _).le

st hd1
    have hnn : 0 ≤ RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt d := by
      rw [RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt]
      by_cases hp : d.Prime
      · simp [hp]
      · simp only [hp, if_false]
        exact vonMangoldt_nonneg
    have h2 : ((N / d : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) := Nat.cast_div_le
    have h3 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ((hw d hd).trans h2) hnn
    have hid : RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt d * ((N : ℝ) / (d : ℝ))
        = (N : ℝ) * (RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt d / (d : ℝ)) := by
      field_simp
    rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg hnn]
    linarith [h3, hid.le, hid.ge]
  refine le_trans (Finset.sum_le_sum hstep) ?_
  rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
  have hN0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg N
  calc (N : ℝ) * ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt d / (d : ℝ)
      ≤ (N : ℝ) * (8 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (RHTower.Mertens.tail_bounded N) hN0
    _ = (8 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by ring

/-- **The signed prime-only identity.**  In Halász's recursion the composite prime powers contribute
`O(N)` in total, so

`∑_{m ≤ N} f(m) log m = ∑_{p ≤ N} f(p) log p · S_f(⌊N/p⌋) + O(N)`.

The values of `f` enter signed: all cancellation among them is preserved. -/
theorem norm_sum_Icc_mul_log_sub_sum_primes_le (hf : ∀ a b : ℕ, f (a * b) = f a * f b)
    (hbdd : ∀ n : ℕ, ‖f n‖ ≤ 1) (N : ℕ) :
    ‖(∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n * ((Real.log (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ))
        - ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
            ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k‖
      ≤ (8 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by
  classical
  have hrec := sum_mul_log_eq_vonMangoldt hf N
  have hsplit : ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
        ((Λ d : ℝ) : ℂ) * f d * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / d), f k
      = (∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
            ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k)
        + ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt d : ℝ) : ℂ) *
            (f d * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / d), f k) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_filter, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun d _ => ?_
    rw [RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt]
    by_cases hp : d.Prime
    · rw [if_pos hp, if_pos hp, vonMangoldt_apply_prime hp]
      push_cast
      ring
    · rw [if_neg hp, if_neg hp]
      ring
  have htail : ‖∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt d : ℝ) : ℂ) *
      (f d * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / d), f k)‖
      ≤ (8 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by
    refine norm_sum_notPrimeVonMangoldt_weight_le _ fun d _ => ?_
    rw [norm_mul]
    calc ‖f d‖ * ‖∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / d), f k‖
        ≤ 1 * ((N / d : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
          mul_le_mul (hbdd d) (norm_sum_Icc_le hbdd _) (norm_nonneg _) zero_le_one
      _ = ((N / d : ℕ) : ℝ) := one_mul _
  rw [hrec, hsplit, add_sub_cancel_left]
  exact htail

/-- **The entry point of the Halász method.**  For a bounded completely multiplicative `f`,

`S_f(N) log N = ∑_{p ≤ N} f(p) log p · S_f(⌊N/p⌋) + O(N)`,

with the explicit constant `9 + mertensTail`.  Every ingredient is elementary: the divisor swap,
`∑_{d ∣ m} Λ(d) = log m`, Stirling's lower bound for `log N!`, and Chebyshev's `ψ − θ`.  Decay of `S_f`
is therefore equivalent to cancellation in the prime sum on the right — and no Dirichlet polynomial of
length `N` and no mean-value theorem at a short height occurs anywhere in the statement. -/
theorem norm_sum_Icc_mul_log_sub_sum_primes_le' (hf : ∀ a b : ℕ, f (a * b) = f a * f b)
    (hbdd : ∀ n : ℕ, ‖f n‖ ≤ 1) (N : ℕ) :
    ‖(∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
        - ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
            ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k‖
      ≤ (9 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by
  classical
  have h1 := norm_sum_Icc_mul_log_sub_le hbdd N
  have h2 := norm_sum_Icc_mul_log_sub_sum_primes_le hf hbdd N
  have hid : (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
        - ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
            ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k
      = ((∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
            - ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n * ((Real.log (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ))
        + ((∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n * ((Real.log (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ))
            - ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
                ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k) := by
    ring
  rw [hid]
  refine le_trans (norm_add_le _ _) ?_
  have hexp : (9 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ)
      = (N : ℝ) + (8 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by ring
  rw [hexp]
  linarith

end RHTower.Sieve

/-!
# Restricting a cochain to the link of a face

Garland's method reads a `k`-cochain through the links of the `(k-1)`-faces: over a face `σ` the
cochain becomes the function `u ↦ f(σ ∪ {u})` on the vertices of the link, and the coboundary of `f`
on `σ ∪ {u, u'}` contains the difference of the two link values.  The sign that makes this work is
the incidence sign of `u` in `σ ∪ {u}`, and the reason it works is the antisymmetry of the incidence
sign under erasing two vertices in the two orders.

* `linkRestrict` : **the restriction of a cochain to the link of a face.**
* `coboundary_link_pair` : **the two link terms of the coboundary are a sign times the difference of
  the link values.**
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [LinearOrder α]

/-- **The restriction of a cochain to the link of a face**: the value on `σ ∪ {u}`, signed so that
the two link terms of the coboundary combine into a difference. -/
def linkRestrict (f : Finset α → ℝ) (σ : Finset α) (u : α) : ℝ :=
  faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u * f (insert u σ)

omit [LinearOrder α] in
theorem erase_insert_insert_left {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu : u ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u') :
    (insert u (insert u' σ)).erase u = insert u' σ := by
  refine Finset.erase_insert ?_
  rw [Finset.mem_insert]
  exact fun hc => hc.elim h hu

omit [LinearOrder α] in
theorem erase_insert_insert_right {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu' : u' ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u') :
    (insert u (insert u' σ)).erase u' = insert u σ := by
  rw [Finset.erase_insert_of_ne h, Finset.erase_insert hu']

theorem linkRestrict_eq {σ : Finset α} (f : Finset α → ℝ) (u : α) :
    f (insert u σ) = faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u * linkRestrict f σ u := by
  rw [linkRestrict, ← mul_assoc, faceSign_mul_self, one_mul]

/-- **The two link terms of the coboundary combine into a difference of link values.**  For a face
`σ ∪ {u, u'}` the summands of `δf` indexed by `u` and `u'` differ by the incidence-sign
antisymmetry, so their sum is a single sign times `f_σ(u) − f_σ(u')`. -/
theorem coboundary_link_pair {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu : u ∉ σ) (hu' : u' ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u')
    (f : Finset α → ℝ) :
    faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u * f (insert u' σ)
        + faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u' * f (insert u σ)
      = (faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u' * faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u)
        * (linkRestrict f σ u - linkRestrict f σ u') := by
  set τ : Finset α := insert u (insert u' σ) with hτ
  have huτ : u ∈ τ := Finset.mem_insert_self _ _
  have hu'τ : u' ∈ τ := Finset.mem_insert_of_mem (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)
  have hanti := faceSign_mul_faceSign_erase_antisymm (F := ℝ) huτ hu'τ h
  rw [erase_insert_insert_left hu h, erase_insert_insert_right hu' h] at hanti
  have hAP : faceSign ℝ τ u * faceSign ℝ (insert u' σ) u'
      = -(faceSign ℝ τ u' * faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u) :=
    eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_left hanti
  rw [linkRestrict_eq (σ := σ) f u, linkRestrict_eq (σ := σ) f u']
  rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, hAP]
  ring

/-- **The coboundary of a cochain, localized at a face.**  On `σ ∪ {u, u'}` the coboundary splits
into the link difference at `σ` and the terms indexed by the vertices of `σ` itself. -/
theorem coboundary_link_decomp {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu : u ∉ σ) (hu' : u' ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u')
    (f : Finset α → ℝ) :
    simplicialCoboundary ℝ f (insert u (insert u' σ))
      = (faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u' * faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u)
          * (linkRestrict f σ u - linkRestrict f σ u')
        + ∑ v ∈ σ, faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) v
            * f ((insert u (insert u' σ)).erase v) := by
  have hmem : u ∉ insert u' σ := by
    rw [Finset.mem_insert]
    exact fun hc => hc.elim h hu
  rw [simplicialCoboundary_apply, Finset.sum_insert hmem, Finset.sum_insert hu',
    erase_insert_insert_left hu h, erase_insert_insert_right hu' h, ← add_assoc,
    coboundary_link_pair hu hu' h f]


end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-!
# G-CE exact-debt cancellation and source-erasure dichotomy

The singular coupled-error wall carries the scalar boundary charge

`d = continuedXiAntiCausalWardResponse (1 / 2)`

and exact graph debt `|d|²`.  This file classifies every bounded complex-linear controller on that
scalar physical channel.

There is one unconditional visible cancellation: the opposite controller `T = -I`.  It sends
`d + T d` to zero and restores the ordinary four-unit Hardy--Fisher wall.  The cancellation is not
free or source-selective.  The controller has energy `|d|²`, and a balanced sum/difference mixer
transfers the complete two-port energy `2|d|²` to the hidden antisymmetric port.

More sharply, one-dimensional complex linearity proves the exhaustive dichotomy

`d + T d = 0  ↔  RH ∨ T = -I`.

Thus every nonerasing scalar linear cancellation is already RH.  The only unconditional branch is
universal erasure of the complete scalar Ward channel.  This rules out scalar physical
cancellation as an independent escape from the G-CE source problem; a successful producer must
act before scalarization or prove that the complementary port vanishes.
-/

open Complex Matrix
open scoped ComplexOrder

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- A scalar boundary controller erases the complete source channel when its visible coherent sum
with every possible input is zero. -/
def mobiusGammaXiDebtControllerErasesSource (T : ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ z : ℂ, z + T z = 0

/-- Unique bounded complex-linear controller which cancels every scalar boundary charge. -/
def mobiusGammaXiOppositeDebtController : ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ :=
  -(ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ ℂ)

/-- In one complex dimension, complete coherent erasure is exactly the opposite controller. -/
theorem mobiusGammaXiDebtControllerErasesSource_iff_eq_opposite
    (T : ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) :
    mobiusGammaXiDebtControllerErasesSource T ↔
      T = mobiusGammaXiOppositeDebtController := by
  constructor
  · intro hT
    apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
    intro z
    have h := hT z
    simp only [mobiusGammaXiOppositeDebtController, _root_.neg_apply,
      ContinuousLinearMap.id_apply]
    linear_combination h
  · rintro rfl
    intro z
    simp [mobiusGammaXiOppositeDebtController]

/-- The opposite controller erases the scalar channel unconditionally. -/
theorem mobiusGammaXiOppositeDebtController_erasesSource :
    mobiusGammaXiDebtControllerErasesSource
      mobiusGammaXiOppositeDebtController := by
  exact
    (mobiusGammaXiDebtControllerErasesSource_iff_eq_opposite _).2 rfl

/-- Actual G-CE scalar charge left in the visible port after applying a boundary controller. -/
def mobiusGammaXiControlledCriticalResidual (T : ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) : ℂ :=
  mobiusGammaXiCoupledErrorCriticalCoefficient +
    T mobiusGammaXiCoupledErrorCriticalCoefficient

/-- Squared singular-graph debt retained by the controlled visible port. -/
def mobiusGammaXiControlledSingularGraphDebt (T : ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) : ℝ :=
  Complex.normSq (mobiusGammaXiControlledCriticalResidual T)

/-- **Exact scalar-controller dichotomy.**  Cancelling the actual G-CE charge either proves RH or
erases every possible scalar source value. -/
theorem mobiusGammaXiDebtController_cancellation_iff_rh_or_erasure
    (T : ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ) :
    mobiusGammaXiControlledCriticalResidual T = 0 ↔
      RiemannHypothesis ∨ mobiusGammaXiDebtControllerErasesSource T := by
  let d := mobiusGammaXiCoupledErrorCriticalCoefficient
  constructor
  · intro hcancel
    by_cases hd : d = 0
    · left
      exact continuedXiAntiCausalWardResponse_half_eq_zero_iff_rh.mp
        (by simpa [d, mobiusGammaXiCoupledErrorCriticalCoefficient] using hd)
    · right
      intro z
      have hTd : T d = -d := by
        dsimp only [mobiusGammaXiControlledCriticalResidual, d] at hcancel
        linear_combination hcancel
      have hzd : ((z / d) : ℂ) • d = z := by
        simp [smul_eq_mul, hd]
      rw [← hzd, map_smul, hTd]
      simp
  · rintro (hRH | herase)
    · have hd : mobiusGammaXiCoupledErrorCriticalCoefficient = 0 := by
        exact continuedXiAntiCausalWardResponse_half_eq_zero_iff_rh.mpr hRH
      simp [mobiusGammaXiControlledCriticalResidual, hd]

# Hermitian-source orientation no-go for reflected BM currents

The literal polarized second-harmonic source supplies the real weight

classification forces a nonreal reflected cancellation ratio on every Xi fibre.  These two laws
are compatible only on the critical wall, where the angular mixing coefficient and hence both

Thus the literal norm-square source cannot generate missing off-wall Peierls orientation.  The
strongest survivor is an exact RH receiver: its reflected current vanishes precisely on the wall.

/-- Literal Hermitian weight transported by the angular--Einstein second-harmonic source. -/

/-- The literal reflected source weights obey the forced complex orientation law. -/
def d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceOrientationCompatible
    (n : ℕ) (q : XiZeroCopy) : Prop :=
  ((d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceWeight
      (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q) : ℝ) : ℂ) =
    ((d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceWeight q : ℝ) : ℂ) *
      d4BMXiReflectionComplexCancellationRatio n q

/-- Literal Hermitian source orientation matches complex cancellation only where source dies. -/
theorem d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceOrientationCompatible_iff
    (n : ℕ) (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceOrientationCompatible n q ↔
      (q.1 : ℂ).re = 1 / 2 := by
  constructor
  · intro hcompat
    by_contra hline
    have hmix : d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient q ≠ 0 :=
      (d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient_eq_zero_iff q).not.mpr hline
    have hcarrier :
        d4ThetaHawkingSelfDualQuadraticCarrierCoefficient 1 (xiSpectralPoint q) ≠ 0 :=
      d4ThetaHawkingSelfDualQuadraticCarrierCoefficient_xi_ne_zero one_ne_zero q
    have hamp : d4BMXiSecondHarmonicPolarizedSourceAmplitude 1 q ≠ 0 := by
      exact mul_ne_zero hmix hcarrier
    have hweight : d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceWeight q ≠ 0 := by
      unfold d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceWeight
      exact (Complex.normSq_eq_zero.not).2 hamp
    have him := congrArg Complex.im hcompat
    simp only [Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.mul_im, Complex.ofReal_re,
      zero_mul, add_zero] at him
    have hratio := d4BMXiReflectionComplexCancellationRatio_im_ne_zero n q
    have hwzero := (mul_eq_zero.mp him.symm).resolve_right hratio
    exact hweight hwzero
  · intro hline
    have hmix : d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient q = 0 :=
      (d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient_eq_zero_iff q).mpr hline
    have hmixr :
        d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient
          (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q) = 0 := by
      rw [d4ThetaTeukolskyOrthogonalHelicityMixingCoefficient_reflect]
      exact hmix
    simp [d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceOrientationCompatible,
      d4BMXiSecondHarmonicHermitianSourceWeight,
      d4BMXiSecondHarmonicPolarizedSourceAmplitude, hmix, hmixr]

theorem hbXiPhaseSensitiveUnitRadiativeSourceFECocycle_transport

        (starRingEnd ℂ)

  rw [d4BMMixedHorizonOpticalSourceProjection_one_eq_green_mul_literalSource,
    d4BMMixedHorizonOpticalSourceProjection_one_eq_green_mul_literalSource,
    hbXiPhaseSensitiveUnitRadiativeSourceFECocycle, map_mul]

    (map_ne_zero (starRingEnd ℂ)).mpr (d4BMGaugeFixedSecondHarmonicGreen_ne_zero q)

    hbXiPhaseSensitiveUnitRadiativeSourceFECocycle,
    xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv_apply_apply, map_div₀, map_mul]
  have hGq := d4BMGaugeFixedSecondHarmonicGreen_ne_zero q
  have hGR := d4BMGaugeFixedSecondHarmonicGreen_ne_zero (xiZeroCopyReflectEquiv q)
  have hstarGq : (starRingEnd ℂ) (d4BMGaugeFixedSecondHarmonicGreen q) ≠ 0 :=
    (map_ne_zero (starRingEnd ℂ)).mpr hGq

      (starRingEnd ℂ)

# Finite Signed Even Frequency Atoms Are Not Markov

- **ID:** finite-signed-even-frequency-atoms-not-markov
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / source-transfer guardrail
- **Grade:** BRIDGE / guardrail. Door-2 reduces the proof to finite
  exponential-sum dominance, so this is not a native theorem. Its use is to
  exclude a false source-transfer shape.
- **Source:** `positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md`;
  `source-selector-repair-obligation-ledger.md`;
  `seam-log-markov-pick-rh-equivalence.md`
- **Statement:** A nonzero finite signed sum of real FE-even exponential
  frequency germs cannot produce a Markov/Stieltjes moment sequence in the
  seam-square coordinate. Its shifted moments are negative on infinitely many
  indices.

## Setup

Let `n>=1`, and let

`0 < lambda_1 < ... < lambda_n`

and let `c_1,...,c_n` be real coefficients with `c_n != 0`. Equal frequencies
are first combined, so the displayed top coefficient is nonzero. Define

`L(z)=sum_{j=1}^n c_j (cosh(lambda_j sqrt(z))-1)`.

For `k>=1`, define the shifted seam moments

`T_k=-2k(-1)^k [z^k]L(z)`.

Set `x_j=lambda_j^2`.

## Theorem

If the signed frequency sum is nonzero, then there are infinitely many `k` for
which

`T_k < 0`.

Consequently `(T_k)_{k>=1}` is not the moment sequence of a positive Borel
measure on `R_+`. In particular, the finite signed real FE-even frequency atom
span intersects the Markov/Stieltjes target only at zero.

## Proof

The coefficient calculation gives

`[z^k]L(z)=sum_{j=1}^n c_j lambda_j^(2k)/(2k)!`

and hence

`T_k = (-1)^(k+1) (sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j^k)/(2k-1)!`.

Let

`S_k=sum_{j=1}^n c_j x_j^k`.

Since `0 < x_1 < ... < x_n`,

`S_k / x_n^k = c_n + sum_{j<n} c_j (x_j/x_n)^k -> c_n`.

Thus, for all sufficiently large `k`, `S_k` has the sign of `c_n`.

If `c_n>0`, then for every sufficiently large even `k`,

`T_k = - S_k/(2k-1)! < 0`.

If `c_n<0`, then for every sufficiently large odd `k`,

`T_k = S_k/(2k-1)! < 0`.

In either case infinitely many shifted moments are negative. Since every moment
of a positive measure on `R_+` is nonnegative, no positive Markov/Stieltjes
representation exists.

Exploratory numerical work, 2026-09-05. Results are not proof certificates.     rw [RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt]
    by_cases hp : d.Prime
    · rw [if_pos hp, if_pos hp, vonMangoldt_apply_prime hp]
      push_cast
      ring
    · rw [if_neg hp, if_neg hp]
      ring
  have htail : ‖∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ((RHTower.Mertens.notPrimeVonMangoldt d : ℝ) : ℂ) *
      (f d * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / d), f k)‖
      ≤ (8 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by
    refine norm_sum_notPrimeVonMangoldt_weight_le _ fun d _ => ?_
    rw [norm_mul]
    calc ‖f d‖ * ‖∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / d), f k‖
        ≤ 1 * ((N / d : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
          mul_le_mul (hbdd d) (norm_sum_Icc_le hbdd _) (norm_nonneg _) zero_le_one
      _ = ((N / d : ℕ) : ℝ) := one_mul _
  rw [hrec, hsplit, add_sub_cancel_left]
  exact htail

/-- **The entry point of the Halász method.**  For a bounded completely multiplicative `f`,

`S_f(N) log N = ∑_{p ≤ N} f(p) log p · S_f(⌊N/p⌋) + O(N)`,

with the explicit constant `9 + mertensTail`.  Every ingredient is elementary: the divisor swap,
`∑_{d ∣ m} Λ(d) = log m`, Stirling's lower bound for `log N!`, and Chebyshev's `ψ − θ`.  Decay of `S_f`
is therefore equivalent to cancellation in the prime sum on the right — and no Dirichlet polynomial of
length `N` and no mean-value theorem at a short height occurs anywhere in the statement. -/
theorem norm_sum_Icc_mul_log_sub_sum_primes_le' (hf : ∀ a b : ℕ, f (a * b) = f a * f b)
    (hbdd : ∀ n : ℕ, ‖f n‖ ≤ 1) (N : ℕ) :
    ‖(∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
        - ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
            ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k‖
      ≤ (9 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by
  classical
  have h1 := norm_sum_Icc_mul_log_sub_le hbdd N
  have h2 := norm_sum_Icc_mul_log_sub_sum_primes_le hf hbdd N
  have hid : (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
        - ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
            ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k
      = ((∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n) * ((Real.log (N : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ)
            - ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n * ((Real.log (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ))
        + ((∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n * ((Real.log (n : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ))
            - ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N with Nat.Prime p,
                ((Real.log (p : ℝ) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f p * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (N / p), f k) := by
    ring
  rw [hid]
  refine le_trans (norm_add_le _ _) ?_
  have hexp : (9 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ)
      = (N : ℝ) + (8 + RHTower.Mertens.mertensTail) * (N : ℝ) := by ring
  rw [hexp]
  linarith

end RHTower.Sieve

end
