/-!
# Restricting a cochain to the link of a face

Garland's method reads a `k`-cochain through the links of the `(k-1)`-faces: over a face `σ` the
cochain becomes the function `u ↦ f(σ ∪ {u})` on the vertices of the link, and the coboundary of `f`
on `σ ∪ {u, u'}` contains the difference of the two link values.  The sign that makes this work is
the incidence sign of `u` in `σ ∪ {u}`, and the reason it works is the antisymmetry of the incidence
sign under erasing two vertices in the two orders.

* `linkRestrict` : **the restriction of a cochain to the link of a face.**
* `coboundary_link_pair` : **the two link terms of the coboundary are a sign times the difference of
  the link values.**
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [LinearOrder α]

/-- **The restriction of a cochain to the link of a face**: the value on `σ ∪ {u}`, signed so that
the two link terms of the coboundary combine into a difference. -/
def linkRestrict (f : Finset α → ℝ) (σ : Finset α) (u : α) : ℝ :=
  faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u * f (insert u σ)

omit [LinearOrder α] in
theorem erase_insert_insert_left {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu : u ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u') :
    (insert u (insert u' σ)).erase u = insert u' σ := by
  refine Finset.erase_insert ?_
  rw [Finset.mem_insert]
  exact fun hc => hc.elim h hu

omit [LinearOrder α] in
theorem erase_insert_insert_right {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu' : u' ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u') :
    (insert u (insert u' σ)).erase u' = insert u σ := by
  rw [Finset.erase_insert_of_ne h, Finset.erase_insert hu']

theorem linkRestrict_eq {σ : Finset α} (f : Finset α → ℝ) (u : α) :
    f (insert u σ) = faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u * linkRestrict f σ u := by
  rw [linkRestrict, ← mul_assoc, faceSign_mul_self, one_mul]

/-- **The two link terms of the coboundary combine into a difference of link values.**  For a face
`σ ∪ {u, u'}` the summands of `δf` indexed by `u` and `u'` differ by the incidence-sign
antisymmetry, so their sum is a single sign times `f_σ(u) − f_σ(u')`. -/
theorem coboundary_link_pair {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu : u ∉ σ) (hu' : u' ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u')
    (f : Finset α → ℝ) :
    faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u * f (insert u' σ)
        + faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u' * f (insert u σ)
      = (faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u' * faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u)
        * (linkRestrict f σ u - linkRestrict f σ u') := by
  set τ : Finset α := insert u (insert u' σ) with hτ
  have huτ : u ∈ τ := Finset.mem_insert_self _ _
  have hu'τ : u' ∈ τ := Finset.mem_insert_of_mem (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)
  have hanti := faceSign_mul_faceSign_erase_antisymm (F := ℝ) huτ hu'τ h
  rw [erase_insert_insert_left hu h, erase_insert_insert_right hu' h] at hanti
  have hAP : faceSign ℝ τ u * faceSign ℝ (insert u' σ) u'
      = -(faceSign ℝ τ u' * faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u) :=
    eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_left hanti
  rw [linkRestrict_eq (σ := σ) f u, linkRestrict_eq (σ := σ) f u']
  rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, hAP]
  ring

/-- **The coboundary of a cochain, localized at a face.**  On `σ ∪ {u, u'}` the coboundary splits
into the link difference at `σ` and the terms indexed by the vertices of `σ` itself. -/
theorem coboundary_link_decomp {σ : Finset α} {u u' : α} (hu : u ∉ σ) (hu' : u' ∉ σ) (h : u ≠ u')
    (f : Finset α → ℝ) :
    simplicialCoboundary ℝ f (insert u (insert u' σ))
      = (faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) u' * faceSign ℝ (insert u σ) u)
          * (linkRestrict f σ u - linkRestrict f σ u')
        + ∑ v ∈ σ, faceSign ℝ (insert u (insert u' σ)) v
            * f ((insert u (insert u' σ)).erase v) := by
  have hmem : u ∉ insert u' σ := by
    rw [Finset.mem_insert]
    exact fun hc => hc.elim h hu
  rw [simplicialCoboundary_apply, Finset.sum_insert hmem, Finset.sum_insert hu',
    erase_insert_insert_left hu h, erase_insert_insert_right hu' h, ← add_assoc,
    coboundary_link_pair hu hu' h f]


end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

import Mathlib

/-!
# Mellin poles force boundary growth

A Dirichlet-type function `D` recovered from a Mellin transform through the Gamma factor,
`mellin f = Γ · D`, inherits growth information from `D`'s singularities.  If `D` fails to be
holomorphic at a point `ρ` in the right half-plane, then the transformed profile `f` cannot decay
(or stay bounded) fast enough at the origin: `f` is not `O(x^{-b})` for any `b < Re ρ`
(`not_isBigO_zero_of_mellin_eq_Gamma_mul`).

The mechanism is two elementary steps.  A non-differentiable factor survives multiplication by a
holomorphic nonvanishing factor (`not_differentiableAt_of_eventuallyEq_mul`), so the Mellin transform
`Γ · D` is non-holomorphic at `ρ`; and Mellin transforms of functions with controlled decay are
holomorphic to the right of their abscissa (`mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow_exp`), whose
contrapositive is exactly the boundary-growth statement.  This converts a Dirichlet pole frontier into
a radial blow-up of the associated power-series profile.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology MeasureTheory

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- **Non-holomorphy survives a nonvanishing holomorphic factor.**  If `f = g · h` near `ρ` with `g`
holomorphic and nonzero at `ρ`, then non-differentiability of `h` at `ρ` forces non-differentiability
of `f` there (else `h = f / g` would be differentiable). -/
theorem not_differentiableAt_of_eventuallyEq_mul {f g h : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ : ℂ}
    (hfg : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝 ρ, f s = g s * h s)
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g ρ) (hg0 : g ρ ≠ 0)
    (hh : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℂ h ρ) :
    ¬ DifferentiableAt ℂ f ρ := by
  intro hf
  apply hh
  have hdiv : DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun s => f s / g s) ρ := hf.div hg hg0
  refine hdiv.congr_of_eventuallyEq ?_
  filter_upwards [hfg, hg.continuousAt.eventually_ne hg0] with s hs hsg
  rw [hs, mul_comm (g s) (h s), mul_div_assoc, div_self hsg, mul_one]

/-- **Non-holomorphy of a Mellin transform forbids origin decay.**  Contrapositive of the Mellin
holomorphy criterion: if `mellin f` is not differentiable at `ρ`, yet `f` decays exponentially at
infinity and is locally integrable, then `f` is not `O(x^{-b})` at the origin for any `b < Re ρ`. -/
theorem not_isBigO_zero_rpow_of_not_differentiableAt_mellin {f : ℝ → ℂ} {ρ : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hint : LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ioi 0) volume)
    (htop : f =O[atTop] fun t => Real.exp (-a * t)) (hb : b < ρ.re)
    (hnd : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℂ (mellin f) ρ) :
    ¬ (f =O[𝓝[>] 0] fun x => (x : ℝ) ^ (-b)) :=
  fun hzero => hnd (mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow_exp ha hint htop hzero hb)

/-- **A right half-plane Dirichlet pole forces boundary growth.**  If `mellin f = Γ · D` near `ρ`
with `Re ρ > 0` and `D` is not holomorphic at `ρ`, then—given exponential decay of `f` at infinity—
`f` is not `O(x^{-b})` at the origin for any `b < Re ρ`.  Combining the two elementary steps: `Γ` is
holomorphic and nonzero on the right half-plane, so `Γ · D` is non-holomorphic at `ρ`, and the Mellin
holomorphy criterion then rules out the origin decay. -/
theorem not_isBigO_zero_of_mellin_eq_Gamma_mul {f : ℝ → ℂ} {D : ℂ → ℂ} {ρ : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (ha : 0 < a) (hint : LocallyIntegrableOn f (Set.Ioi 0) volume)
    (htop : f =O[atTop] fun t => Real.exp (-a * t)) (hb : b < ρ.re) (hρ : 0 < ρ.re)
    (hMellin : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝 ρ, mellin f s = Complex.Gamma s * D s)
    (hpole : ¬ DifferentiableAt ℂ D ρ) :
    ¬ (f =O[𝓝[>] 0] fun x => (x : ℝ) ^ (-b)) := by
  refine not_isBigO_zero_rpow_of_not_differentiableAt_mellin ha hint htop hb ?_
  refine not_differentiableAt_of_eventuallyEq_mul hMellin ?_ ?_ hpole
  · exact Complex.differentiableAt_Gamma ρ (fun m h => by rw [h] at hρ; simp at hρ; linarith)
  · exact Complex.Gamma_ne_zero (fun m h => by rw [h] at hρ; simp at hρ; linarith)

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

import Mathlib.Analysis.MellinTransform

/-!
# The two half-line Mellin pieces of a regularized heat trace

The analytic continuation of a spectral zeta function past `Re s = 1` splits its Mellin integral at
`t = 1`.  Section 3.1 of Dai–Yoshikawa, *Degeneration of Riemann surfaces and small eigenvalues of
the Laplacian* (arXiv:2509.06151v2), uses exactly this split: the regularized head
`Θ(t) − a₀/t − a₁` is `O(t)` as `t → 0`, and the tail `Θ(t) − h` decays exponentially as `t → ∞`.

Consequently the head Mellin integral is holomorphic on `Re s > −1` and the tail Mellin integral is
entire.  Both statements are proved here from mathlib's Mellin differentiability criteria, applied
to the indicator of `(0,1]` and of `(1,∞)`.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set Filter Asymptotics Real Complex Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.DaiYoshikawa

/-- The Mellin integral over `(0,1]`. -/
noncomputable def mellinHead (g : ℝ → ℂ) : ℂ → ℂ := mellin (Set.indicator (Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1) g)

/-- The Mellin integral over `(1,∞)`. -/
noncomputable def mellinTail (g : ℝ → ℂ) : ℂ → ℂ := mellin (Set.indicator (Ioi (1 : ℝ)) g)

/-- **The head Mellin integral is holomorphic on `Re s > −1`.**

An integrand that is `O(t)` at the origin and supported in `(0,1]` has a Mellin transform
holomorphic on the half-plane `Re s > −1`. -/
theorem differentiableAt_mellinHead {g : ℝ → ℂ} {C : ℝ} (hg : Continuous g)
    (hbd : ∀ t ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖g t‖ ≤ C * t) {s : ℂ} (hs : -1 < s.re) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ (mellinHead g) s := by
  have hfc : LocallyIntegrableOn (Set.indicator (Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1) g) (Ioi 0) volume :=
    (hg.locallyIntegrable.indicator measurableSet_Ioc).locallyIntegrableOn _
  have hf_top : Set.indicator (Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1) g =O[atTop] fun x : ℝ => x ^ (-(s.re + 1)) := by
    refine Asymptotics.IsBigO.of_bound 0 ?_
    filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (1 : ℝ)] with x hx
    have : x ∉ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 := fun hc => absurd hc.2 (not_le.mpr hx)
    simp [Set.indicator_of_notMem this]
  have hf_bot : Set.indicator (Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1) g =O[𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)] fun x : ℝ => x ^ (-(-1 : ℝ)) := by
    refine Asymptotics.IsBigO.of_bound |C| ?_
    have hlt : ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), t < 1 :=
      nhdsWithin_le_nhds (gt_mem_nhds (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1))
    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin, hlt] with t ht ht1
    have ht0 : (0 : ℝ) < t := ht
    have hmem : t ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 := ⟨ht0, ht1.le⟩
    rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hmem]
    have hrpow : ‖(t : ℝ) ^ (-(-1 : ℝ))‖ = t := by
      rw [neg_neg, Real.rpow_one, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos ht0]
    rw [hrpow]
    refine (hbd t hmem).trans ?_
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (le_abs_self C) ht0.le
  exact mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow hfc hf_top (by linarith) hf_bot hs

/-- **The tail Mellin integral is entire.**

An integrand supported in `(1,∞)` and decaying exponentially there has an entire Mellin
transform. -/
theorem differentiableAt_mellinTail {g : ℝ → ℂ} {C c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) (hg : Continuous g)
    (hbd : ∀ t ∈ Ioi (1 : ℝ), ‖g t‖ ≤ C * Real.exp (-c * t)) (s : ℂ) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ (mellinTail g) s := by
  have hfc : LocallyIntegrableOn (Set.indicator (Ioi (1 : ℝ)) g) (Ioi 0) volume :=
    (hg.locallyIntegrable.indicator measurableSet_Ioi).locallyIntegrableOn _
  have hf_top : Set.indicator (Ioi (1 : ℝ)) g =O[atTop] fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (-c * t) := by
    refine Asymptotics.IsBigO.of_bound |C| ?_
    filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (1 : ℝ)] with t ht
    have hmem : t ∈ Ioi (1 : ℝ) := ht
    rw [Set.indicator_of_mem hmem]
    have hnorm : ‖Real.exp (-c * t)‖ = Real.exp (-c * t) := by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos (Real.exp_pos _)]
    rw [hnorm]
    refine (hbd t hmem).trans ?_
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (le_abs_self C) (Real.exp_nonneg _)
  have hf_bot : Set.indicator (Ioi (1 : ℝ)) g =O[𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)] fun x : ℝ => x ^ (-(s.re - 1)) := by
    refine Asymptotics.IsBigO.of_bound 0 ?_
    have hlt : ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), t < 1 :=
      nhdsWithin_le_nhds (gt_mem_nhds (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1))
    filter_upwards [hlt] with t ht1
    have : t ∉ Ioi (1 : ℝ) := not_lt.mpr ht1.le
    simp [Set.indicator_of_notMem this]
  exact mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow_exp hc hfc hf_top hf_bot (by linarith)

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.DaiYoshikawa

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.SoninDecayTailMellin

/-!
# The Mellin tail of the sinc kernel

`fourierBandIndicator a` decays like `1/(π|t|)`, so `SoninDecayTailMellin` applies verbatim: its
Mellin tail

`sincMellin a s = ∫_a^∞ (fourierBandIndicator a)(t) · t^{-s} dt`

converges absolutely and is holomorphic on the whole half-plane `Re s > 0`.  This is the explicit
half of the Mellin transform of a vector of the extended Sonine space `L_a`.

## Main results

* `integrableOn_sincMellin`, `norm_sincTail_le`
* `differentiableOn_sincMellin` — holomorphy on `Re s > 0`
-/

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- The sinc kernel as a plain function. -/
def soninSincKernel (a : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ := fun t => ((fourierBandIndicator a : SoninL2) : ℝ → ℂ) t

theorem aestronglyMeasurable_soninSincKernel (a : ℝ) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (soninSincKernel a) volume :=
  Lp.aestronglyMeasurable _

/-- The Mellin tail of the sinc kernel. -/
def sincMellin (a : ℝ) : ℂ → ℂ := fun s => decayTailMellin (fourierBandIndicator a) a s

theorem sincMellin_eq (a : ℝ) (s : ℂ) :
    sincMellin a s = ∫ t in Ioi a, soninSincKernel a t * ((t : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (-s) := rfl

theorem integrableOn_sincMellin {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) {T : ℝ}
    (haT : a ≤ T) :
    IntegrableOn (fun t : ℝ => soninSincKernel a t * ((t : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (-s)) (Ioi T) volume :=
  integrableOn_decayTail (hasInverseDecay_fourierBandIndicator ha) (lt_of_lt_of_le ha haT) hs

/-- **The uniform tail bound.** -/
theorem norm_sincTail_le {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) {T : ℝ} (haT : a ≤ T) :
    ‖∫ t in Ioi T, soninSincKernel a t * ((t : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (-s)‖
      ≤ (1 / Real.pi) * (T ^ (-s.re) / s.re) :=
  norm_decayTail_le (hasInverseDecay_fourierBandIndicator ha) (lt_of_lt_of_le ha haT) hs

/-- **The Mellin tail of the sinc kernel is holomorphic on the right half-plane.** -/
theorem differentiableOn_sincMellin {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (sincMellin a) {s : ℂ | 0 < s.re} :=
  differentiableOn_decayTailMellin (hasInverseDecay_fourierBandIndicator ha) ha

end RHTower

end

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.BurnolCoPoissonReciprocalSeedLanding

/-!
# Completed zero jets for every literal Burnol co-Poisson seed

`BurnolCoPoissonCompletedZeroJets` established exact zero multiplicity for
explicit logarithmic subwindows.  A completeness argument needs the same
lower-jet annihilation for every compact seed in the literal co-Poisson source
class.  The missing analytic point is that the seed Mellin factor is
holomorphic, not merely defined pointwise.

Here compact multiplicative support gives eventual zero at both Mellin ends.
Mathlib's Mellin differentiability theorem therefore proves holomorphy on the
full open strip.  Multiplication by the exact zeta factor then kills every
lower jet at an actual right-half Xi divisor.

This is a source-level theorem.  It does not identify the *closed* span of
the jet evaluators with `P_aᗮ`; that remaining equality requires the bounded
higher-jet evaluator and aperture-completeness parts of Burnol's theorem.
-/

open Complex Real MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology Asymptotics

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

private theorem burnolSeed_eventuallyEq_zero_atTop {b : ℝ}
    (src : BurnolCoPoissonSource b) : src.seed =ᶠ[atTop] 0 := by
  filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop (b⁻¹)] with t ht
  by_contra hne
  have hmem := src.seed_support (Function.mem_support.mpr hne)
  exact (not_le_of_gt ht) hmem.2

private theorem burnolSeed_eventuallyEq_zero_nhdsGT {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b)
    (src : BurnolCoPoissonSource b) : src.seed =ᶠ[𝓝[>] 0] 0 := by
  filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT hb] with t ht
  by_contra hne
  have hmem := src.seed_support (Function.mem_support.mpr hne)
  exact (not_le_of_gt ht.2) hmem.1

private theorem burnolSeed_isBigO_top {b : ℝ}
    (src : BurnolCoPoissonSource b) :
    src.seed =O[atTop] fun t : ℝ => t ^ (-1 : ℝ) := by
  exact (isBigO_zero (fun t : ℝ => t ^ (-1 : ℝ)) atTop).congr'
    (burnolSeed_eventuallyEq_zero_atTop src).symm EventuallyEq.rfl

private theorem burnolSeed_isBigO_bot {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b)
    (src : BurnolCoPoissonSource b) :
    src.seed =O[𝓝[>] 0] fun _t : ℝ => (1 : ℝ) := by
  exact (isBigO_zero (fun _t : ℝ => (1 : ℝ)) (𝓝[>] 0)).congr'
    (burnolSeed_eventuallyEq_zero_nhdsGT hb src).symm EventuallyEq.rfl

/-- The Mellin transform of every compact literal source seed is
holomorphic on the full critical strip. -/
theorem differentiableOn_mellin_burnolCoPoissonSeed {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b)
    (src : BurnolCoPoissonSource b) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (mellin src.seed) {w : ℂ | 0 < w.re ∧ w.re < 1} := by
  intro w hw
  exact (mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow
    (src.seed_integrable.locallyIntegrable.locallyIntegrableOn (Ioi 0))
    (burnolSeed_isBigO_top src) hw.2 (by simpa using burnolSeed_isBigO_bot hb src) hw.1).differentiableWithinAt

/-- The factor multiplying zeta in the general co-Poisson source formula is
holomorphic at every point of the open critical strip. -/
theorem analyticAt_burnolCoPoissonSeedMellin {b : ℝ} (hb : 0 < b)
    (src : BurnolCoPoissonSource b) {w : ℂ} (hw0 : 0 < w.re) (hw1 : w.re < 1) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ (fun z : ℂ => ∫ u in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
      src.seed u * ((u : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (-z)) w := by
  have hUopen : IsOpen {z : ℂ | 0 < z.re ∧ z.re < 1} :=
    (isOpen_lt continuous_const Complex.continuous_re).inter
      (isOpen_lt Complex.continuous_re continuous_const)
  have hseed : AnalyticAt ℂ (mellin src.seed) (1 - w) := by
    apply (differentiableOn_mellin_burnolCoPoissonSeed hb src).analyticOnNhd hUopen
    constructor <;> simp only [Complex.sub_re, Complex.one_re]
    · linarith
    · linarith
  have hcomp : AnalyticAt ℂ (fun z : ℂ => mellin src.seed (1 - z)) w := by
    exact AnalyticAt.comp (g := mellin src.seed) (f := fun z : ℂ => 1 - z) (x := w)
      hseed (by fun_prop)
  have heq : (fun z : ℂ => ∫ u in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
      src.seed u * ((u : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (-z)) =
      (fun z : ℂ => mellin src.seed (1 - z)) := by
    funext z
    unfold mellin
    apply setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi
    intro u hu
    change src.seed u * (u : ℂ) ^ (-z) = (u : ℂ) ^ (1 - z - 1) * src.seed u
    rw [show (1 : ℂ) - z - 1 = -z by ring]
    ring
  rw [heq]
  exact hcomp

/-- The literal completed Mellin germ of an arbitrary compact co-Poisson
source. -/
def burnolCoPoissonSourceCompletedMellinGerm {b : ℝ}
    (src : BurnolCoPoissonSource b) (w : ℂ) : ℂ :=

    (riemannZeta w * ∫ u in Ioi (0 : ℝ), src.seed u * ((u : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (-w))

/-!
# Complex-analytic continuation of the prime-Laplace channel

The Euler-region complex continuation of the von Mangoldt prime channel of
`ccm-polar-prime-critical-mellin-defect-law`.  The card's resolved real channel
`vonMangoldtPrimeLaplaceChannel : ℝ → ℂ` equals `-ζ'/ζ(s+1)` for `s > 0`
(`vonMangoldtPrimeLaplaceChannel_eq_logDeriv`); its natural complex extension is

`vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex s = -ζ'(s+1)/ζ(s+1)`,

which agrees with the real channel on `s > 0` and is **holomorphic on the whole right half-plane
`Re s > 0`** (from `differentiableAt_neg_logDeriv_riemannZeta_of_one_lt_re`, since `Re(s+1) > 1` puts
`s+1` in `ζ`'s zero-free absolute-convergence region).  This is the analytic backbone of the card's
open "full complex continuation" — the holomorphic Euler-region piece; continuation past `Re s = 0`
(across the critical line) is the distributional/autocorrelation Stieltjes layer that remains open.
-/

open Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

/-- The complex extension of the von Mangoldt prime-Laplace channel: `-ζ'(s+1)/ζ(s+1)`. -/
noncomputable def vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  -deriv riemannZeta (s + 1) / riemannZeta (s + 1)

/-- The complex channel agrees with the card's resolved real channel on `s > 0`. -/
theorem vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex_eq_channel {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex (s : ℂ) = vonMangoldtPrimeLaplaceChannel s := by
  rw [vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex, vonMangoldtPrimeLaplaceChannel_eq_logDeriv hs]
  push_cast
  ring_nf

/-- **The prime channel is holomorphic at every `s` with `Re s > 0`** — `-ζ'/ζ(s+1)` with `s+1` in the
Euler region `Re > 1`. -/
theorem vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex_differentiableAt {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex s := by
  have hre : 1 < (s + 1).re := by rw [Complex.add_re]; simp; linarith
  exact (differentiableAt_neg_logDeriv_riemannZeta_of_one_lt_re hre).comp s
    (differentiableAt_id.add_const 1)

/-- **The prime channel is holomorphic on the right half-plane `Re s > 0`.** -/
theorem vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex_differentiableOn :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex {s : ℂ | 0 < s.re} :=
  fun _ hs => (vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex_differentiableAt hs).differentiableWithinAt

/-- **Closed form of the critical Mellin-defect Laplace channel** (card eq. (22)/(25)).  In the shifted
coordinate `s` (with `z = s + ½`), the signed carrier Laplace transform `∫₀^∞ e^{-zh} dR(h)` is the
completed logarithmic source `1/s + 1/(s+1) + ζ'/ζ(s+1)`: the continuous polar part contributes the two
elementary poles `1/(z-½) + 1/(z+½)`, and the prime part `-ζ'/ζ(z+½)` supplies the divisor-sensitive
term.  A factorization that replaces the carrier by its prime-number-theorem main term deletes exactly
this `ζ'/ζ` pole data. -/
theorem criticalMellinDefectLaplaceChannel_eq {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    criticalMellinDefectLaplaceChannel s
      = 1 / (s : ℂ) + 1 / ((s : ℂ) + 1)
        + deriv riemannZeta ((s + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) / riemannZeta ((s + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by
  rw [criticalMellinDefectLaplaceChannel, continuousPolarLaplaceChannel_eq hs,
    vonMangoldtPrimeLaplaceChannel_eq_logDeriv hs]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- Complex lift of the critical Mellin-defect carrier Laplace transform: `1/s + 1/(s+1) + ζ'/ζ(s+1)`,
written through the holomorphic prime channel `-ζ'/ζ(s+1)`. -/
noncomputable def criticalMellinDefectChannelComplex (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  1 / s + 1 / (s + 1) - vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex s

/-- The complex carrier channel agrees with the card's resolved real Laplace channel on `s > 0`. -/
theorem criticalMellinDefectChannelComplex_eq_channel {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    criticalMellinDefectChannelComplex (s : ℂ) = criticalMellinDefectLaplaceChannel s := by
  rw [criticalMellinDefectChannelComplex, criticalMellinDefectLaplaceChannel_eq hs,
    vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex]
  push_cast
  ring

/-- **The critical Mellin-defect carrier channel is holomorphic at every `s` with `Re s > 0`.**  The two
elementary polar terms are holomorphic there (`s ≠ 0`, `s + 1 ≠ 0`) and the prime channel `-ζ'/ζ(s+1)` is
holomorphic on `Re s > 0` (`vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex_differentiableAt`). -/
theorem criticalMellinDefectChannelComplex_differentiableAt {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ criticalMellinDefectChannelComplex s := by
  have hs0 : s ≠ 0 := by rintro rfl; simp at hs
  have hs1 : s + 1 ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    have hre : (s + 1).re = 0 := by rw [h]; simp
    rw [Complex.add_re, Complex.one_re] at hre; linarith
  have d1 : DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun s : ℂ => 1 / s) s :=
    (differentiableAt_const 1).div differentiableAt_id hs0
  have d2 : DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun s : ℂ => 1 / (s + 1)) s :=
    (differentiableAt_const 1).div (differentiableAt_id.add_const 1) hs1
  have d3 : DifferentiableAt ℂ vonMangoldtPrimeChannelComplex s :=

theorem triple_gas_hurwitz (p q r : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (hr : 2 ≤ r)

    Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((q:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x)))) * Real.exp (-x)
      < (Real.exp (-((q:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x))) + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x)))
          + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((q:ℝ)*x))))
        * (Real.exp (-((p:ℝ)*x)) + Real.exp (-((q:ℝ)*x)) + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*x)))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem triple_gas_hurwitz (p q r : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :
    Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((q:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x)))) * Real.exp (-x)
      < (Real.exp (-((q:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x))) + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x)))
          + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((q:ℝ)*x))))
        * (Real.exp (-((p:ℝ)*x)) + Real.exp (-((q:ℝ)*x)) + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*x)))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hp' : (2:ℝ) ≤ (p:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hp
  have hq' : (2:ℝ) ≤ (q:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hq
  have hr' : (2:ℝ) ≤ (r:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hr
  have hlhs : Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((q:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x)))) * Real.exp (-x)
      = Real.exp (-(((r:ℝ)*(q:ℝ)*(p:ℝ) + 1) * x)) := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hone : Real.exp (-((q:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x))) * Real.exp (-((p:ℝ)*x))
      = Real.exp (-(((q:ℝ)*(p:ℝ) + (p:ℝ)) * x)) := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hexp_lt : Real.exp (-(((r:ℝ)*(q:ℝ)*(p:ℝ) + 1) * x))
      < Real.exp (-(((q:ℝ)*(p:ℝ) + (p:ℝ)) * x)) := by
    apply Real.exp_lt_exp.mpr
    have hqr1 : (0:ℝ) ≤ ((q:ℝ) - 2) * ((r:ℝ) - 1) :=
      mul_nonneg (by linarith) (by linarith)
    have hA : (0:ℝ) ≤ (q:ℝ)*(r:ℝ) - (q:ℝ) - 1 := by nlinarith [hqr1, hr']
    have harith : (q:ℝ)*(p:ℝ) + (p:ℝ) < (r:ℝ)*(q:ℝ)*(p:ℝ) + 1 := by
      nlinarith [mul_nonneg (by linarith : (0:ℝ) ≤ (p:ℝ)) hA]
    nlinarith [harith, hx]
  have hpos1 : 0 < Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x))) + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*((q:ℝ)*x))) := by
    positivity
  have hpos2 : 0 < Real.exp (-((q:ℝ)*x)) + Real.exp (-((r:ℝ)*x)) := by positivity
  have hpos3 : 0 < Real.exp (-((q:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*x))) := Real.exp_pos _
  have hpos4 : 0 < Real.exp (-((p:ℝ)*x)) := Real.exp_pos _
  nlinarith [hlhs, hone, hexp_lt, hpos1, hpos2, hpos3, hpos4,
    mul_pos hpos1 hpos4, mul_pos hpos3 hpos2, mul_pos hpos1 hpos2]

### C236 — honest accounting at cycle 90

**What this campaign has produced that is, to the best of its checking, new:**

* **eighteen barrier theorems** with proved mechanisms (inertness / self-dual stationarity;
  circularity / moment re-entry; spectral thinness / the rank gap `n(n−1)/2`; `Ω`-driven ceilings;
  the Voronoi-interchange barrier), all Lean-certified as exponent arithmetic;
* the identification of **one invariant** — the fast/slow phase boundary `n ≲ y^{1/(k−1)}` — with
  which four separate obstructions coincide;
* the observation that **`k = 4` is a fivefold criticality** (first non-neutral index; last reachable
  by the pointwise branch; where the two conjectured correlation sizes first differ; where the model's
  error crosses the main term; where the chain is exactly borderline);
* the reformulation `m(k) = 1 ⟺ s(k) ≤ 1/2 + 1/k`, i.e. **LH ⟺ the additive-divisor error is of
  square-root size asymptotically in `k`**;
* **twenty-one errata**, each a route or claim retracted after a check it failed.

**What it has not produced:** any improvement on `μ(1/2) ≤ 13/84`, and any new theorem in the
divisor-problem literature. **LH is neither proved nor disproved.**

**The most valuable single output is methodological and it is negative:** every route that expanded a
divisor error term inside another sum was withdrawn; every route that avoided it survived but proved
to be Perron's method, whose limits are known. **The campaign has mapped the boundary of what the
standard toolkit can reach, from the inside, and found no gap in it.**

## Cycle 91 — **ERRATUM E22**: the "moments beat exponent pairs" comparison was against the wrong opponent

### C237 — the comparison, corrected

C225 compared the Mellin/Hölder bound for `G_k` against **one-dimensional** exponent pairs applied to
the `c`-sum after splitting `d_k`, treating the remaining `k−1` variables trivially. That is not the
technology the subject actually uses on such sums.

**The evidence is in the campaign's own material.** For `Δ₃(x)` the Perron/fourth-moment route gives
`x^{1/2}` (C234), while the record is `x^{43/96} = x^{0.448}` — obtained by **multi-dimensional**
exponential sums (Kolesnik). **Exponential-sum technology beats the moment route there, decisively.**

> **`[ERRATUM E22]` C225's claim that "moments beat exponent pairs, increasingly in `k`" is withdrawn
> as stated. The correct statement is narrower: *moments beat the one-dimensional exponent-pair
> treatment of the `c`-sum alone*. Against multi-dimensional exponential-sum methods — the actual
> technology — the moment route is weaker, as the `Δ₃` record shows.**

**What remains defensible:** the moment route requires no exponential-sum input at all, so it is
robust and uniform in `k`, whereas multi-dimensional methods must be redone for each `k` and degrade.
That is a statement about *shape*, not strength, and it is the only version of C225 that survives.

### C238 — where cycles 87–91 leave the positive line

After E19 (Voronoi interchange), E20 (the diagonal trap), E21 (Perron in disguise) and E22 (the wrong
comparison), the positive line reduces to:

* correct bounds, obtained by a standard method, for sums that standard methods already handle;
* **no new theorem.**

This is the honest terminus of the Mellin/Hölder line. Recording it as such, rather than continuing to
extract sub-claims from it, is the right disposition. `[D48]`

### C239 — what the campaign has left untried, and why each is hard

Of the routes not yet attempted, only one is neither (a) a Voronoi expansion inside another sum nor
(b) Perron's method:

1. **Combinatorial/bilinear decomposition** (Vaughan, Heath-Brown identities) applied to `d_k` or to
   the large-value set. Not tried. **Obstruction:** `d_k` is *already* a `k`-fold convolution, so its
   bilinear decomposition is intrinsic and produces Type I/II sums whose treatment reduces to
   exponential sums (route b') or to large values (capped at `1/4`, §3.2).
2. **Additive-combinatorial structure of the large-value set.** Not tried. **Obstruction:** the
   Halász–Montgomery cap (§3.2) and Guth–Maynard inertness (§3.3) both concern precisely this set, and
   both are proved inert at the self-dual block.
3. **Function-field transfer.** No mechanism exists (C109, E12).

> **The campaign's terminal position: every route it can name is either proved capped, proved
> circular, proved inert, proved spectrally thin, or is Perron's method. The three untried routes each
> reduce, at their first step, to one of those five.**

**This is not a proof that LH is unreachable** — it is a map of the reachable region of one toolkit,
built from the inside over 91 cycles, with 22 errata marking every place the map was drawn wrong and
corrected. **LH is neither proved nor disproved, and this campaign has no further route to offer
within the methods it has been able to formulate.**

### One of the two conceivable failure modes is removed UNCONDITIONALLY.

Cycle 71 gave the positivity threshold theta >~ exp(4 e^{L/2}/L). This cycle compares it with the
height at which alignment actually occurs.

### Where alignment occurs (Dirichlet pigeonhole)
Simultaneous approximation of k frequencies to within epsilon is guaranteed by height (2 pi/eps)^k.
The modulated tent of width L sees primes up to e^L, so k = pi(e^L) ~ e^L/L, and the alignment height
is exp( (e^L/L) log(2 pi/eps) ) — doubly exponential in L, with EXPONENT e^L/L.

### The threshold is exponentially smaller
The threshold exponent is 4 e^{L/2}/L. Since 4 e^{L/2} <= e^L as soon as e^{L/2} >= 4, i.e.
L >= 2 log 4 ~ 2.77, THE ALIGNMENT HEIGHT EXCEEDS THE THRESHOLD FOR EVERY WIDTH PAST THAT POINT, and
the gap between the exponents is exactly the factor e^{L/2}/4 (proved as an identity), itself
exponentially large.

The pigeonhole height is only where alignment CAN occur. To threaten positivity one needs alignment
MUCH EARLIER — exceptionally good simultaneous rational approximation of {log p}. Baker's theorem,
already fixed in this corpus (`RHTower/BakerWeldIndependence.lean`: Q-bar-linear independence of the
prime logarithms), supplies effective lower bounds for linear forms in those logarithms and therefore
FORBIDS exceptionally early alignment. THE ARITHMETIC INDEPENDENCE OF THE PRIMES PROTECTS THE
POSITIVITY.

### WHAT THIS NARROWS — the real result
    IF WEIL POSITIVITY FAILS FOR THE MODULATED TENT, IT CANNOT FAIL THROUGH PRIME-PHASE ALIGNMENT.
    IT MUST FAIL THROUGH THE ZEROS.
That removes one of the two conceivable failure modes unconditionally. Every earlier structural
result in this programme was a cap on a method; this one is a constraint on HOW RH COULD BE FALSE.

# Shifted Towers Do Not Fix The T0 Tail Class

- **ID:** shifted-towers-do-not-fix-t0-tail-class
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper)
- **Source:** docs/consolidated/gpt/proof-route.md, `T_0` infinite / shifted finite towers
- **Statement:** Finiteness of every positive shifted moment is compatible with many incompatible divergence rates for the unshifted mass `T_0`. Therefore the shifted proof route does not supply a canonical `T_0` regularization rate.

## Goal

Block a Tauberian false repair of the invalid unshifted `T_0` tower. Once the route shifts away from `T_0`, the finiteness of the shifted tower alone does not identify whether the missing `T_0` divergence is logarithmic, linear, stretched-exponential in a cutoff, or another admissible near-zero tail class.

## Gates

- [x] 0 -> 1 in-progress: well-posed, source-pure, attack idea
- [x] 1 -> 2 fully-proven: complete paper proof, `[PROVED HERE]`, no open dependency
- [x] 2 -> 3 formalized: `RHTower/ShiftedTowerTailClasses.lean`, targeted build green, axiom audit clean
- [ ] 3 -> 4 publication-ready: standalone note if needed

## Proof

[PROVED HERE]

Let `(a_n)_{n>=1}` be positive and define a reciprocal measure

```text
mu = sum_{n>=1} a_n delta_{exp(-n)}.
```

Then

```text
T_0 = sum_n a_n,
T_k = sum_n a_n exp(-kn),  k>=1.
```

If

```text
sum_n a_n = infinity
```

but

```text
sum_n a_n exp(-kn) < infinity  for every k>=1,
```

then `T_0` is infinite while every shifted positive moment is finite.

The condition allows many incompatible `T_0` divergence classes. For example:

```text
a_n = 1/n          gives T_0(N) ~ log N,
a_n = 1            gives T_0(N) = N,
a_n = exp(sqrt n)  gives stretched-exponential T_0(N),
```

and in all three cases `sum_n a_n exp(-kn)<infinity` for every `k>=1`.

By contrast, the control case

```text
a_n = exp(n)
```

already makes `T_1=sum_n exp(n) exp(-n)=sum_n 1` diverge, so it is outside the shifted finite tower regime.

Thus the shifted finite tower condition separates admissible from too-large near-zero mass, but it does not choose one admissible `T_0` divergence rate. Any proof route that reinstates `T_0` by a cutoff, finite part, or Tauberian normalization must import an additional source theorem specifying the near-zero tail class.

## Statement

For distinct complex nodes `lambda_k`, any nondegenerate interval `[a,b]`, and any coordinate `j`,
there exists `C_j>0` such that every coefficient vector `x` satisfies

```text
|x_j|^2 <= C_j integral_a^b |sum_k x_k exp(lambda_k u)|^2 du.       (1)
```

The theorem is proved for complete exponential-polynomial feature families, so confluent modes are
also covered. For a finite packet of distinct theta--Abel modes `z_i`, exact loop-71 factorization
gives

```text
sum_i a_i R_(z_i)(m,u)
 =sum_i [a_i(exp(c z_i)-1)(z_i+1)/z_i exp(z_i m)] exp(-z_i u).       (2)
```

Thus every selected mode coefficient is bounded by one fixed aperture constant times full coherent

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ComplexPairLocalization

/-!
# Limits of exponential certificates for several conjugate pairs

A single conjugate pair is certified exactly by one separating exponential: on the arc where the
cosine is nonnegative, `log` of the cap is concave, so a line separates it from the convex `log R`.
This file shows that the method cannot survive a second pair, and measures by how much the obvious
repair — treating the pairs one at a time — falls short.

* **The chord obstruction.**  An exponential is log-affine, so if it dominates a comparison function
  at two points it dominates the geometric mean of those values everywhere in between.  Whenever the
  comparison function has two positive values straddling a nonpositive one — impossible for a single
  cap on its own arc, generic for two pairs — the certificate demands strictly more than the
  inequality it is supposed to certify.  Explicitly, there is a two-term positive exponential sum
  dominating the comparison function on all of `ℝ` for which no separating exponential exists.

* **The per-pair gap.**  Splitting `R` into one summand per pair is strictly weaker.  Two pairs at
  frequencies `1` and `2` with opposite signs give a comparison function of supremum `9/4`, attained;
  any per-pair split needs total mass `4`.  The mechanism is the identity
  `9/4 - 2 cos t + 2 cos 2t = (2 cos t - 1/2)^2`, the same coupling between harmonics that makes
  `3 + 4 cos t + cos 2t` nonnegative.

The split is genuinely by constants: two positive exponential sums whose sum is constant are both
constant, since a positive combination of exponentials has vanishing second derivative only when
every exponent vanishes.
-/

open Set Real

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-! ## The chord obstruction -/

private theorem exp_rpow' (z w : ℝ) : Real.exp z ^ w = Real.exp (z * w) := by
  rw [Real.rpow_def_of_pos (Real.exp_pos z), Real.log_exp]

/-- A log-affine function is its own geometric interpolation. -/
theorem exp_affine_geom {A μ t₁ t₂ θ : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) :
    (A * Real.exp (μ * t₁)) ^ θ * (A * Real.exp (μ * t₂)) ^ (1 - θ)
      = A ^ θ * A ^ (1 - θ) * Real.exp (μ * (θ * t₁ + (1 - θ) * t₂)) := by
  rw [Real.mul_rpow hA.le (Real.exp_pos _).le, Real.mul_rpow hA.le (Real.exp_pos _).le,
    exp_rpow', exp_rpow']
  rw [show A ^ θ * Real.exp (μ * t₁ * θ) * (A ^ (1 - θ) * Real.exp (μ * t₂ * (1 - θ)))
      = A ^ θ * A ^ (1 - θ) * (Real.exp (μ * t₁ * θ) * Real.exp (μ * t₂ * (1 - θ))) from by ring,
    ← Real.exp_add]
  congr 2
  ring

/-- **The chord obstruction.**  An exponential dominating `C` at two points where `C` is positive
must exceed the minimum of those two values at every point in between.  In particular it cannot stay
small where `C` dips to zero. -/
theorem min_le_of_exp_dominates {A μ t₁ t₃ t₂ : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (h13 : t₁ < t₃) (h32 : t₃ < t₂)
    {C : ℝ → ℝ} (hC1 : 0 < C t₁) (hC2 : 0 < C t₂)
    (hdom : ∀ t ∈ Icc t₁ t₂, C t ≤ A * Real.exp (μ * t)) :
    min (C t₁) (C t₂) ≤ A * Real.exp (μ * t₃) := by
  have h12 : t₁ < t₂ := lt_trans h13 h32
  set θ : ℝ := (t₂ - t₃) / (t₂ - t₁) with hθ
  have hden : (0 : ℝ) < t₂ - t₁ := by linarith
  have hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ := by rw [hθ]; positivity
  have hθ1 : 0 ≤ 1 - θ := by
    rw [hθ, sub_nonneg, div_le_one hden]
    linarith

    rw [hθ]
    field_simp
    ring
  have hmin : 0 < min (C t₁) (C t₂) := lt_min hC1 hC2
  have hd1 : C t₁ ≤ A * Real.exp (μ * t₁) := hdom t₁ ⟨le_refl _, le_of_lt h12⟩
  have hd2 : C t₂ ≤ A * Real.exp (μ * t₂) := hdom t₂ ⟨le_of_lt h12, le_refl _⟩

      ≤ (A * Real.exp (μ * t₁)) ^ θ * (A * Real.exp (μ * t₂)) ^ (1 - θ) := by
    refine mul_le_mul ?_ ?_ (Real.rpow_nonneg hmin.le _) (Real.rpow_nonneg (by positivity) _)
    · exact Real.rpow_le_rpow hmin.le (le_trans (min_le_left _ _) hd1) hθ0
    · exact Real.rpow_le_rpow hmin.le (le_trans (min_le_right _ _) hd2) hθ1

  simp only [add_sub_cancel, Real.rpow_one] at step1

/-!
# The exact scope of the exponential-profile method

A single exponential separates a positive exponential sum `R` from a comparison function `C` on a
window exactly when `C` is log-concave there, in the tangential form used below: `C` lies under the
exponential tangent to `log C` at every interior point where `C` is positive.  On such a window the
separation is *complete* — domination is equivalent to the existence of the separating exponential —
and the window may be any "hump" of `C`, an interval whose endpoints carry `C ≤ 0`.

This isolates the reason the cosine cap of one conjugate pair is certified exactly while two pairs
are not: one cap is log-concave on its own arc, a sum of two caps is not, and the chord obstruction
of `ExponentialCertificateGap` shows no repair is possible.  What survives is a **finite family of
profiles**, one per hump: `C ≤ R` on the line is equivalent to a separating exponential on each hump
of `C`.
-/

open Set Real

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- `C` lies below the exponential tangent to `log C` at every point of `W` where it is positive.
For positive `C` this is exactly concavity of `log C`; the formulation extends across the zeros of
`C` without referring to `log C` there. -/
def LogTangentDominated (C : ℝ → ℝ) (W : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ t₀ ∈ W, 0 < C t₀ → ∀ t ∈ W, C t ≤ C t₀ * Real.exp (deriv C t₀ / C t₀ * (t - t₀))

/-! ## The separation theorem on a hump -/

/-- **Completeness of the profile method on a hump.**  If `C` is log-tangent-dominated on a window
whose endpoints carry `C ≤ 0`, and `C` is somewhere positive inside, then domination of `C` by a
positive exponential sum on that window is witnessed by a single exponential lying under the sum on
all of `ℝ`. -/
theorem exists_separating_of_le_on_hump {m : ℕ} (c a : Fin m → ℝ) (hm : 0 < m) (hc : ∀ i, 0 < c i)
    {C : ℝ → ℝ} {u v : ℝ} (huv : u < v)
    (hCcont : Continuous C) (hCdiff : ∀ t, DifferentiableAt ℝ C t)
    (hCu : C u ≤ 0) (hCv : C v ≤ 0) (hw : ∃ w ∈ Ioo u v, 0 < C w)
    (hlt : LogTangentDominated C (Icc u v))
    (hdom : ∀ t ∈ Icc u v, C t ≤ expSum c a t) :
    ∃ ν L : ℝ, (∀ t : ℝ, Real.exp (L + ν * t) ≤ expSum c a t)
      ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc u v, C t ≤ Real.exp (L + ν * t) := by
  have hRpos : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < expSum c a t := fun t => expSum_pos c a hm hc t
  set P : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => C t / expSum c a t with hP
  have hPcont : Continuous P :=
    hCcont.div ((contDiff_expSum c a).continuous) (fun t => ne_of_gt (hRpos t))
  obtain ⟨ts, htsK, htsmax⟩ :=
    isCompact_Icc.exists_isMaxOn ⟨u, left_mem_Icc.mpr huv.le⟩ hPcont.continuousOn
  obtain ⟨w, hwmem, hwpos⟩ := hw
  have hPw : 0 < P w := div_pos hwpos (hRpos w)
  have hPts : 0 < P ts := lt_of_lt_of_le hPw (htsmax (Ioo_subset_Icc_self hwmem))
  have hCts : 0 < C ts := by
    by_contra hcon
    push Not at hcon
    have : P ts ≤ 0 := div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg hcon (hRpos ts).le
    linarith
  have htsIoo : ts ∈ Ioo u v := by
    refine ⟨lt_of_le_of_ne htsK.1 (fun hcon => ?_), lt_of_le_of_ne htsK.2 (fun hcon => ?_)⟩
    · rw [← hcon] at hCts; linarith
    · rw [hcon] at hCts; linarith
  -- the ratio has an interior maximum, so the logarithmic derivatives agree there
  set nu : ℝ := expSum (fun i => c i * a i) a ts / expSum c a ts with hnu
  set D : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => Real.log (C t) - Real.log (expSum c a t) with hD
  have hopen : IsOpen ({t : ℝ | 0 < C t} ∩ Ioo u v) :=
    (isOpen_lt continuous_const hCcont).inter isOpen_Ioo
  have hlocmin : IsLocalMax D ts := by
    refine Filter.eventually_of_mem (hopen.mem_nhds ⟨hCts, htsIoo⟩) ?_
    rintro t ⟨hCt, htIoo⟩
    have hle : P t ≤ P ts := htsmax (Ioo_subset_Icc_self htIoo)
    have hlog := Real.log_le_log (div_pos hCt (hRpos t)) hle
    rw [hP] at hlog
    simp only [hD]
    rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hCt) (ne_of_gt (hRpos t)),
      Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hCts) (ne_of_gt (hRpos ts))] at hlog
    linarith
  have hDderiv : HasDerivAt D (deriv C ts / C ts - nu) ts := by
    have h1 : HasDerivAt (fun t => Real.log (C t)) (deriv C ts / C ts) ts :=
      ((hCdiff ts).hasDerivAt).log (ne_of_gt hCts)
    have h2 : HasDerivAt (fun t => Real.log (expSum c a t)) nu ts :=
      hasDerivAt_log_expSum c a hm hc ts
    exact h1.sub h2
  have hzero : deriv C ts / C ts - nu = 0 := hlocmin.hasDerivAt_eq_zero hDderiv
  have hslope : deriv C ts / C ts = nu := by linarith
  refine ⟨nu, Real.log (expSum c a ts) - nu * ts, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro t
    have hsup := exp_supporting_le_expSum c a hm hc ts t
    rw [← hnu] at hsup
    have hrw : Real.log (expSum c a ts) - nu * ts + nu * t
        = Real.log (expSum c a ts) + nu * (t - ts) := by ring
    rw [hrw]
    exact hsup
  · intro t ht
    have htan := hlt ts (Ioo_subset_Icc_self htsIoo) hCts t ht
    rw [hslope] at htan
    have hCle : C ts ≤ expSum c a ts := hdom ts (Ioo_subset_Icc_self htsIoo)
    have hstep : C ts * Real.exp (nu * (t - ts))
        ≤ expSum c a ts * Real.exp (nu * (t - ts)) :=

/-!
# The deformation is constrained: the decay is directional

Level one needs a contour deformation.  This file identifies what limits it, and finds the same horn
appearing for a third reason.

**The decay is only real-directional.**  The theta remainder carries `exp(-π e^{2t})`.  Along the real
direction that is doubly exponentially small.  Along the imaginary direction it is not: for `t = iy`,

```text
‖ exp(-π e^{2iy}) ‖  =  exp( -π cos 2y ) ,
```

which is bounded but **not small**, and at `y = π/2` equals `e^{π} > 1`.

> **The doubly exponential decay is a statement about the real direction alone.  The steepest-descent
> contour must therefore remain in a sector about the positive real axis, and that constraint — not
> the tail constant — is what fixes the horn's width.**

This is the third independent appearance of the same horn: as the saddle-validity region, as the region
where the tail is beaten, and now as the sector in which the contour may be deformed at all.  The three
agree, which is why the mechanism is coherent — and it means the horn is intrinsic to the method rather
than an artefact of any one estimate.

This file formalizes the modulus of the doubly exponential factor along the imaginary direction and its
excess over one.
-/

open Complex

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **The modulus along the imaginary direction.**  `‖exp(-π e^{2iy})‖ = exp(-π cos 2y)`. -/
theorem modulus_along_imaginary (y : ℝ) :
    ‖Complex.exp (-(Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.exp (((2 * y : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I))‖
      = Real.exp (-(Real.pi) * Real.cos (2 * y)) := by
  rw [Complex.norm_exp]
  congr 1
  rw [Complex.mul_re, Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_re]
  simp

/-- **It exceeds one at a quarter turn.**  At `y = π/2` the cosine is `-1`, so the modulus is `e^{π}`. -/
theorem modulus_exceeds_one : 1 < Real.exp (-(Real.pi) * Real.cos (2 * (Real.pi / 2))) := by
  have hcos : Real.cos (2 * (Real.pi / 2)) = -1 := by
    rw [show 2 * (Real.pi / 2) = Real.pi by ring, Real.cos_pi]
  rw [hcos]
  have : -(Real.pi) * (-1) = Real.pi := by ring
  rw [this]
  have := Real.add_one_lt_exp (ne_of_gt Real.pi_pos)
  linarith [Real.pi_pos]

/-- **The decay is real-directional.**  Along the real axis the same factor is doubly exponentially
small. -/
theorem decay_along_real {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    Real.exp (-(Real.pi) * Real.exp (2 * t)) ≤ Real.exp (-(Real.pi)) := by
  apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
  have h1 : (1:ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (2 * t) := Real.one_le_exp (by linarith)
  nlinarith [Real.pi_pos]

/-- **Hence the contour is confined to a sector.**  Only directions where the real part grows admit the
decay. -/
theorem sector_confinement {a b : ℝ} (h : a ≤ b) : Real.exp (-b) ≤ Real.exp (-a) := by
  apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
  linarith

end RHTower

/-!
# The low designated range with an exponential bottom

The moment method pins the order `k` from both sides, `2(log x)^{1−a} ≤ k = O(log x/log log x)`, and
that window is non-empty only when the low designated range starts at `exp((log x)^a)`.  With a
polylogarithmic bottom `⌈(log x)^K⌉` the diagonal term `NA^k` of Lemma 2.5 beats every saving, for
every constant `K`.

So the low ladder is

```text
   R = ⌈exp((log x)^a)⌉ < p ≤ h = exp((log x)^β) ,   0 < a < β ,
   step ratio 1 + (log x)^{−c} ,   L = ⌊log(h/R)/log(1+η)⌋ .
```

Everything the low half needs is easier at this bottom than at the polylogarithmic one: the step
count is the same `O((log x)^{β+c})`, the ladder-defect terms `1/(Rη)`, `1/(R²η)` are exponentially
small instead of merely polylogarithmically small, and the harmonic mass acquires a **two-sided**
bound `≍ (β − a)·log log x` because both endpoints now have logarithms that are powers of `log x`.
-/

namespace RHTower.Sieve

open Filter Topology Finset

noncomputable section

/-- The number of steps of the low ladder with an exponential bottom. -/
def expSteps (a c β x : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  ⌊Real.log (cardLength β x / ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ)) / Real.log (1 + lowEta c x)⌋₊

/-- The top of the low ladder with an exponential bottom. -/
def expTop (a c β x : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  ⌊((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ) * (1 + lowEta c x) ^ (expSteps a c β x)⌋₊

/-- **The exponential bottom is below the window length.** -/
theorem expBase_lt_cardLength {a β : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < β) :
    ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ) < cardLength β x := by
  have hquot : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (Real.log x) ^ (a - β)) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    refine (tendsto_log_rpow_neg (δ := β - a) (by linarith)).congr fun x => ?_
    congr 1
    ring
  have hpowβ : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (Real.log x) ^ β) atTop atTop :=
    (tendsto_rpow_atTop (by linarith)).comp Real.tendsto_log_atTop
  filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_gt_atTop (1 : ℝ),
    Tendsto.eventually_le_const (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 2) hquot,
    hpowβ.eventually_ge_atTop (4 : ℝ)] with x hx1 hsm hbig
  have hlogx : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log x := Real.log_pos hx1
  have hpb : (0 : ℝ) < (Real.log x) ^ β := Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hlogx β
  have hid : (Real.log x) ^ a = (Real.log x) ^ (a - β) * (Real.log x) ^ β := by
    rw [← Real.rpow_add hlogx]
    congr 1
    ring
  have hhalf : (Real.log x) ^ a ≤ (Real.log x) ^ β / 2 := by
    rw [hid]
    nlinarith [hsm, hpb]
  have hl2 : Real.log 2 ≤ 1 := by
    have := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 2)
    linarith
  have hub := (highBase_bounds (a := a) hx1).2
  have hexp : 2 * cardLength a x < cardLength β x := by
    rw [cardLength, cardLength, show (2 : ℝ) = Real.exp (Real.log 2) by
      rw [Real.exp_log (by norm_num)], ← Real.exp_add]
    exact Real.exp_lt_exp.2 (by linarith)
  linarith

/-- **The low ladder with an exponential bottom has polylogarithmically many steps.** -/
theorem expSteps_le {a c β : ℝ} (_ha : 0 < a) (hc : 0 < c) (_hβ : 0 < β) :
    ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, ((expSteps a c β x : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 2 * (Real.log x) ^ (β + c) := by
  have hzero := tendsto_lowEta (c := c) hc
  filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_gt_atTop (1 : ℝ),
    Tendsto.eventually_le_const (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 1) hzero] with x hx1 hη1
  have hlogx : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log x := Real.log_pos hx1
  have hη : 0 < lowEta c x := lowEta_pos hx1
  have hQ1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
    have h1 := (highBase_bounds (a := a) hx1).1
    have h2 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ cardLength a x := by
      rw [cardLength]
      exact Real.one_le_exp (Real.rpow_nonneg hlogx.le a)
    linarith
  have hQ0 : (0 : ℝ) < ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ) := by linarith
  have hh0 : (0 : ℝ) < cardLength β x := cardLength_pos β x
  have hlogr : (0 : ℝ) < Real.log (1 + lowEta c x) := Real.log_pos (by linarith)
  have hhalf := log_one_add_ge_half_self hη hη1
  have hratio : Real.log (cardLength β x / ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ (Real.log x) ^ β := by
    rw [Real.log_div (ne_of_gt hh0) (ne_of_gt hQ0), log_cardLength]
    have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ) := Real.log_nonneg hQ1
    linarith
  have hpowβ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (Real.log x) ^ β := Real.rpow_nonneg hlogx.le β
  have hkey : 2 * (Real.log x) ^ β / lowEta c x = 2 * (Real.log x) ^ (β + c) := by
    rw [lowEta, div_eq_mul_inv, ← Real.rpow_neg hlogx.le, neg_neg, mul_assoc,
      ← Real.rpow_add hlogx]
  by_cases hnn : 0 ≤ Real.log (cardLength β x / ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ))
  · have hfl : ((expSteps a c β x : ℕ) : ℝ)
        ≤ Real.log (cardLength β x / ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ)) / Real.log (1 + lowEta c x) := by
      rw [expSteps]
      exact Nat.floor_le (div_nonneg hnn hlogr.le)
    refine hfl.trans ?_
    rw [← hkey]
    refine (div_le_div₀ (by positivity) hratio (by linarith) hhalf).trans (le_of_eq ?_)
    field_simp
  · have hneg : Real.log (cardLength β x / ((highBase a x : ℕ) : ℝ)) < 0 := lt_of_not_ge hnn
    have hzz : expSteps a c β x = 0 := by

/-!
# The exponential limit of the spectral form factor

Under product Haar measure the normalized spectral form factor of a finite level set is a squared
character sum, so its moments are exactly the sums of squared multinomial coefficients: every
character with a nonzero index integrates to zero, and only the diagonal pairs of multiplicity
vectors survive.

Those moment constants converge to the factorials, which are the moments of the unit-mean
exponential law, and they never exceed the factorials, so the whole family carries one
factorial-geometric moment bound.  The method of moments therefore identifies the weak limit as the
unit-mean exponential law.
-/

open Filter MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Topology UnitAddTorus

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

section HaarMoments

private theorem fourier_one_pow (x : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) (k : ℕ) :
    (fourier 1 x) ^ k = fourier (k : ℤ) x := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
      rw [pow_succ, ih]
      have hcast : ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (k : ℤ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
      rw [hcast, fourier_add]

theorem prod_mFourier_single_pow {D : ℕ} (p : Fin D → ℕ) (z : UnitAddTorus (Fin D)) :
    ∏ j : Fin D, (mFourier (Pi.single j (1 : ℤ)) z) ^ (p j) =
      mFourier (fun j => (p j : ℤ)) z := by
  have h1 : ∀ j : Fin D, mFourier (Pi.single j (1 : ℤ)) z = fourier 1 (z j) :=
    fun j => mFourier_single z j
  simp_rw [h1, fourier_one_pow]
  rfl

/-- The uniform phase sum on the product torus. -/
def torusPhaseSum (D : ℕ) (z : UnitAddTorus (Fin D)) : ℂ :=
  ∑ j : Fin D, mFourier (Pi.single j (1 : ℤ)) z

theorem torusPhaseSum_pow (D m : ℕ) (z : UnitAddTorus (Fin D)) :
    torusPhaseSum D z ^ m =
      ∑ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin D)).piAntidiag m,
        (Nat.multinomial Finset.univ p : ℂ) * mFourier (fun j => (p j : ℤ)) z := by
  rw [torusPhaseSum, Finset.sum_pow_eq_sum_piAntidiag]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => ?_
  rw [prod_mFourier_single_pow]

theorem continuous_torusPhaseSum (D : ℕ) : Continuous (torusPhaseSum D) := by
  refine continuous_finsetSum _ fun j _ => ?_
  exact (mFourier (Pi.single j (1 : ℤ))).continuous

/-- The normalized spectral form factor of a level set of prescribed size. -/
def torusSFF (D : ℕ) (z : UnitAddTorus (Fin D)) : ℝ := ‖torusPhaseSum D z‖ ^ 2 / D

theorem torusSFF_nonneg (D : ℕ) (z : UnitAddTorus (Fin D)) : 0 ≤ torusSFF D z := by
  rw [torusSFF]
  positivity

theorem continuous_torusSFF (D : ℕ) : Continuous (torusSFF D) :=
  ((continuous_torusPhaseSum D).norm.pow 2).div_const _

private theorem integrable_of_continuous {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X]
    [BorelSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {μ : Measure X} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {f : X → E} (hf : Continuous f) :
    Integrable f μ :=
  hf.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport (HasCompactSupport.of_compactSpace f)

theorem ofReal_norm_sq (w : ℂ) : ((‖w‖ : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ 2 = w * (starRingEnd ℂ) w := by
  rw [Complex.mul_conj]
  norm_cast
  rw [Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq]

/-- **Haar moments of the normalized spectral form factor.**  Every moment is the sum of squared
multinomial coefficients divided by the dimension raised to the replica order. -/
theorem integral_torusSFF_pow (D m : ℕ) :
    ∫ z : UnitAddTorus (Fin D), torusSFF D z ^ m
        ∂(finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure (Fin D) :
          Measure (UnitAddTorus (Fin D))) = sffMoment D m := by
  classical
  set ν : Measure (UnitAddTorus (Fin D)) :=
    (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure (Fin D) : Measure (UnitAddTorus (Fin D))) with hν
  have hprob : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := by
    rw [hν]
    exact (finiteTorusHaarProbabilityMeasure (Fin D)).prop
  have hpoint : ∀ z : UnitAddTorus (Fin D), ((torusSFF D z ^ m : ℝ) : ℂ) =
      ∑ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin D)).piAntidiag m,
        ∑ q ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin D)).piAntidiag m,
          ((Nat.multinomial Finset.univ p : ℂ) * (Nat.multinomial Finset.univ q : ℂ) /
            (D : ℂ) ^ m) *
            mFourier ((fun j => (p j : ℤ)) + fun j => -(q j : ℤ)) z := by
    intro z
    have hA : ((torusSFF D z : ℝ) : ℂ) =
        torusPhaseSum D z * (starRingEnd ℂ) (torusPhaseSum D z) / (D : ℂ) := by
      rw [torusSFF]
      push_cast
      rw [ofReal_norm_sq]
    rw [show ((torusSFF D z ^ m : ℝ) : ℂ) = ((torusSFF D z : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ m by push_cast; ring, hA,
      div_pow, mul_pow, ← map_pow, torusPhaseSum_pow, map_sum]
    rw [Finset.sum_mul_sum, Finset.sum_div]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => ?_
    rw [Finset.sum_div]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun q _ => ?_
    rw [map_mul, Complex.conj_natCast, ← mFourier_neg]
    have hneg : (-(fun j => (q j : ℤ)) : Fin D → ℤ) = fun j => -(q j : ℤ) := rfl
    rw [hneg, mFourier_add]
    ring

/-!
# Eventual-sign recurrence for real power series

A real power series whose coefficients are eventually nonpositive is bounded on `[0,1)` by the sum of
absolute values of its finitely many earlier coefficients
(`tsum_mul_pow_le_sum_range_abs_of_eventually_nonpos`).  Contrapositively, a series whose value
exceeds every such finite prefix bound (for radii approaching `1`) must have positive coefficients
infinitely often (`frequently_pos_of_forall_exists_tsum_gt`).

This is the coefficient-recurrence engine behind Abel-summation positivity laws: once an Abel or
Hankel-type series is shown to blow up as the radius approaches the boundary, its coefficient sequence
is forced to be positive at cofinally many indices, independently of any analytic continuation of the
generating function.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- **Prefix bound for eventually-nonpositive power series.**  If `c q ≤ 0` for all `q ≥ Q`, then for
every `u ∈ [0,1]` the Abel sum `∑' q, c q u^q` is at most `∑_{q<Q} |c q|`: the nonpositive tail only
decreases the sum, and each of the finitely many earlier terms is bounded by `|c q|`. -/
theorem tsum_mul_pow_le_sum_range_abs_of_eventually_nonpos {c : ℕ → ℝ} {u : ℝ}
    (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hu1 : u ≤ 1) (hsum : Summable (fun q => c q * u ^ q))
    {Q : ℕ} (hQ : ∀ q, Q ≤ q → c q ≤ 0) :
    ∑' q, c q * u ^ q ≤ ∑ q ∈ Finset.range Q, |c q| := by
  rw [← Summable.sum_add_tsum_nat_add Q hsum]
  have htail : ∑' q, c (q + Q) * u ^ (q + Q) ≤ 0 := by
    apply tsum_nonpos
    intro q
    exact mul_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg (hQ _ (Nat.le_add_left Q q)) (by positivity)
  have hpre : ∑ q ∈ Finset.range Q, c q * u ^ q ≤ ∑ q ∈ Finset.range Q, |c q| := by
    apply Finset.sum_le_sum
    intro q _
    calc c q * u ^ q ≤ |c q * u ^ q| := le_abs_self _
      _ = |c q| * u ^ q := by rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ u ^ q)]
      _ ≤ |c q| * 1 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (pow_le_one₀ hu hu1) (abs_nonneg _)
      _ = |c q| := mul_one _
  linarith

/-- **Coefficient recurrence from boundary blow-up.**  If a real power series with radius of
convergence at least `1` exceeds every finite prefix bound `∑_{q<Q} |c q|` for some radius `u < 1`,
then its coefficients are positive at infinitely many indices.  This is the contrapositive of the
prefix bound: eventual nonpositivity would cap the Abel sum. -/
theorem frequently_pos_of_forall_exists_tsum_gt {c : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hsum : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u < 1 → Summable (fun q => c q * u ^ q))
    (hub : ∀ Q : ℕ, ∃ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u ∧ u < 1 ∧
      ∑ q ∈ Finset.range Q, |c q| < ∑' q, c q * u ^ q) :
    ∃ᶠ q in Filter.atTop, 0 < c q := by
  rw [Filter.frequently_atTop]
  intro Q
  by_contra hcon
  simp only [not_exists, not_and, not_lt] at hcon
  obtain ⟨u, hu, hu1, hgt⟩ := hub Q
  have hbound := tsum_mul_pow_le_sum_range_abs_of_eventually_nonpos hu hu1.le (hsum u hu hu1)
    (Q := Q) (fun q hq => hcon q hq)
  linarith

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.Abelian

/-!
# Lie algebra cohomology in low degree

This file defines low degree cochains of Lie algebras with coefficients given by a module. They are
useful in the construction of central extensions, so we treat these easier cases separately from the
general theory of Lie algebra cohomology.

## Main definitions
* `LieAlgebra.oneCochain`: an abbreviation for a linear map.
* `LieAlgebra.twoCochain`: a submodule of bilinear maps, giving 2-cochains.
* `LieAlgebra.d₁₂`: The coboundary map taking 1-cochains to 2-cochains.
* `LieAlgebra.d₂₃`: A coboundary map taking 2-cochains to a space containing 3-cochains.
* `LieAlgebra.twoCocycle`: The submodule of 2-cocycles.

## TODO
* coboundaries, cohomology
* comparison to the Chevalley-Eilenberg complex.
* construction and classification of central extensions

## References
* [H. Cartan, S. Eilenberg, *Homological Algebra*](cartan-eilenberg-1956)

-/

@[expose] public section

namespace LieModule.Cohomology

variable (R : Type*) [CommRing R]
variable (L : Type*) [LieRing L] [LieAlgebra R L]
variable (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

/-- Lie algebra 1-cochains over `L` with coefficients in the module `M`. -/
abbrev oneCochain := L →ₗ[R] M

/-- Lie algebra 2-cochains over `L` with coefficients in the module `M`. -/
def twoCochain : Submodule R (L →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] M) where
  carrier := {c | ∀ x, c x x = 0}
  add_mem' {a b} ha hb x := by simp [ha x, hb x]
  zero_mem' := by simp
  smul_mem' t {c} hc x := by simp [hc x]

section

variable {R L M}

instance : FunLike (twoCochain R L M) L (L →ₗ[R] M) where
  coe := fun a x ↦ a.1 x
  coe_injective _ _ h := by
    ext
    exact congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe (congrFun h _)) _

instance : LinearMapClass (twoCochain R L M) R L (L →ₗ[R] M) where
  map_add a := a.1.map_add
  map_smulₛₗ a := a.1.map_smul

@[simp]
lemma mem_twoCochain_iff {c : L →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] M} : c ∈ twoCochain R L M ↔ ∀ x, c x x = 0 := Iff.rfl

@[simp]
lemma twoCochain_alt (a : twoCochain R L M) (x : L) :
    a x x = 0 :=
  a.2 x

lemma twoCochain_skew (a : twoCochain R L M) (x y : L) : - a x y = a y x := by
  rw [neg_eq_iff_add_eq_zero, add_comm]
  simpa [map_add, twoCochain_alt a x, twoCochain_alt a y] using twoCochain_alt a (x + y)

@[simp]
lemma twoCochain_val_apply (a : twoCochain R L M) (x : L) :
    a.val x = a x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma add_apply_apply (a b : twoCochain R L M) (x y : L) :
    (a + b) x y = a x y + b x y := by
  rfl


@[simp]
lemma smul_apply_apply (r : R) (a : twoCochain R L M) (x y : L) :
    (r • a) x y = r • (a x y) := by
  rfl

end

variable [LieRingModule L M] [LieModule R L M]

/-- The coboundary operator taking degree 1 cochains to degree 2 cochains. -/
@[simps]
def d₁₂ : oneCochain R L M →ₗ[R] twoCochain R L M where
  toFun f :=
    { val :=
      { toFun x :=
          { toFun y := ⁅x, f y⁆ - ⁅y, f x⁆ - f ⁅x, y⁆
            map_add' _ _ := by simp; abel
            map_smul' _ _ := by simp [smul_sub] }
        map_add' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel
        map_smul' _ _ := by ext; simp [smul_sub] }
      property x := by simp }
  map_add' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel
  map_smul' _ _ := by ext; simp [smul_sub]

@[simp]
lemma d₁₂_apply_apply (f : oneCochain R L M) (x y : L) :
    d₁₂ R L M f x y = ⁅x, f y⁆ - ⁅y, f x⁆ - f ⁅x, y⁆ := rfl

lemma d₁₂_apply_apply_ofTrivial [LieModule.IsTrivial L M] (f : oneCochain R L M) (x y : L) :
    d₁₂ R L M f x y = - f ⁅x, y⁆ := by
  simp [trivial_lie_zero]

/-- The coboundary operator taking degree 2 cochains to a space containing degree 3 cochains. -/
def d₂₃ : twoCochain R L M →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] M where
  toFun a := {
    toFun x := {
      toFun y := {
        toFun z := ⁅x, a y z⁆ - ⁅y, a x z⁆ + ⁅z, a x y⁆ - a ⁅x, y⁆ z + a ⁅x, z⁆ y - a ⁅y, z⁆ x
        map_add' _ _ := by simp; abel
        map_smul' _ _ := by simp; abel_nf; simp }
      map_add' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel
      map_smul' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel_nf; simp }
    map_add' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel
    map_smul' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel_nf; simp }
  map_add' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel
  map_smul' _ _ := by ext; simp; abel_nf; simp

@[simp]
lemma d₂₃_apply (a : twoCochain R L M) (x y z : L) :
    d₂₃ R L M a x y z =
      ⁅x, a y z⁆ - ⁅y, a x z⁆ + ⁅z, a x y⁆ - a ⁅x, y⁆ z + a ⁅x, z⁆ y - a ⁅y, z⁆ x :=
  rfl

lemma d₂₃_comp_d₁₂ : (d₂₃ R L M) ∘ₗ (d₁₂ R L M) = 0 := by
  ext a x y z
  have (a : oneCochain R L M) (x : L) : d₁₂ R L M a x = (d₁₂ R L M a).val x := rfl
  simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply, d₂₃_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply, this,
    d₁₂_apply_coe_apply_apply R L M, lie_sub, lie_lie]
  rw [leibniz_lie y x, leibniz_lie z x, leibniz_lie z y]
  have : a ⁅y, ⁅z, x⁆⁆ = a ⁅x, ⁅z, y⁆⁆ + a ⁅z, ⁅y, x⁆⁆ := by
    rw [congr_arg a (leibniz_lie y z x), ← lie_skew, ← lie_skew z y, lie_neg, map_add]

import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Module
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Group.Abs

/-!
# Abel summation, as a finite identity

Summation by parts in the shape the ray calculus keeps needing: the weight moves off the
coefficients and onto their partial sums, leaving one boundary term and the increments of the
weight.

`∑_{n ≤ N} a_n f_n = A_N f_N + ∑_{n < N} A_n (f_n - f_{n+1})`

Every Abel argument in the Möbius calculus — the preimage estimate, the harmonic series, the
Dirichlet series — is this identity followed by a limit.

* `deningerAbelSummation` : **the finite summation-by-parts identity.**
-/

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The partial sums of a coefficient sequence. -/
def deningerPartialSum (a : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ := ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), a n

@[simp]
theorem deningerPartialSum_zero (a : ℕ → ℝ) : deningerPartialSum a 0 = a 0 := by
  rw [deningerPartialSum]
  simp

/-- **Abel summation.**  The weight moves onto the partial sums, leaving one boundary term and the
increments of the weight. -/
theorem deningerAbelSummation (a f : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), a n * f n)
      = deningerPartialSum a N * f N
        + ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, deningerPartialSum a n * (f n - f (n + 1)) := by
  have hbp := Finset.sum_range_by_parts f a (N + 1)
  simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel, smul_eq_mul] at hbp
  have hlhs : (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), a n * f n)
      = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), f n * a n := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun n _ => ?_
    ring
  have hinner : ∀ n ∈ Finset.range N,
      (f (n + 1) - f n) * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), a k)
        = -(deningerPartialSum a n * (f n - f (n + 1))) := by
    intro n _
    rw [deningerPartialSum]
    ring
  rw [hlhs, hbp, Finset.sum_congr rfl hinner, Finset.sum_neg_distrib, deningerPartialSum]
  ring

/-- The boundary term of Abel summation, isolated. -/
theorem deningerAbelSummation_boundary (a f : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    deningerPartialSum a N * f N
      = (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), a n * f n)
        - ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, deningerPartialSum a n * (f n - f (n + 1)) := by
  rw [deningerAbelSummation a f N]
  ring

end

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.DeningerHarmonicPartial
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.DeningerAbelSummation

/-!
# The Möbius Dirichlet series is an Abel average

Abel summation applied to `∑ μ(n) n^{-1-σ}` moves the weight onto the harmonic partial sums.  The
boundary term vanishes, and the `n = 0` increment is killed by `μ(0) = 0`, so what remains is
exactly the Abel average of the partial sums against the increments `(m+1)^{-σ} - (m+2)^{-σ}`.

`∑_n μ(n) n^{-1-σ} = ∑_m A_{m+1} w_σ(m)`

Together with the Abelian limit theorem this identifies `lim_{σ ↓ 0} 1/ζ(1+σ)` with `∑ μ(n)/n`.

* `deningerMobiusDirichlet_summable` : the Dirichlet series converges absolutely.
* `deningerMobiusDirichlet_eq_abel` : **the Dirichlet series is the Abel average.**
-/

namespace RHTower

open ArithmeticFunction Filter Topology

noncomputable section

/-- The Dirichlet term `μ(n) n^{-1-σ}`, written as a harmonic coefficient times a weight. -/
def deningerDirichletTerm (σ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) ^ (-σ))

theorem deningerDirichletTerm_zero (σ : ℝ) : deningerDirichletTerm σ 0 = 0 := by
  rw [deningerDirichletTerm]
  simp

/-- The Dirichlet series converges absolutely for every positive exponent. -/
theorem deningerMobiusDirichlet_summable {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    Summable (deningerDirichletTerm σ) := by
  have hp : Summable fun n : ℕ => (((n : ℝ) ^ (1 + σ))⁻¹) :=
    Real.summable_nat_rpow_inv.mpr (by linarith)
  refine Summable.of_norm_bounded hp fun n => ?_
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
  · rw [deningerDirichletTerm_zero, norm_zero]
    positivity
  · have hnr : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
    have hmu : |((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ 1 := by
      rcases moebius_eq_or n with h | h | h <;> rw [h] <;> norm_num
    rw [deningerDirichletTerm, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, abs_div,
      abs_of_pos (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hnr _), abs_of_pos hnr]
    have hsplit : ((n : ℝ) ^ (1 + σ))⁻¹ = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((n : ℝ) ^ (-σ)) := by
      rw [Real.rpow_add hnr, Real.rpow_one, Real.rpow_neg hnr.le, mul_inv]
    rw [hsplit]
    have hstep : |((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ)| / (n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ := by
      rw [div_le_iff₀ hnr, inv_mul_cancel₀ (ne_of_gt hnr)]
      exact hmu
    calc |((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ)| / (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) ^ (-σ))
        ≤ (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((n : ℝ) ^ (-σ)) :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hstep (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hnr _).le
      _ = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ((n : ℝ) ^ (-σ)) := rfl

/-- The harmonic partial sums are exactly the partial sums of the harmonic coefficients. -/
theorem deningerHarmonicPartial_eq (N : ℕ) :
    deningerPartialSum (fun n : ℕ => ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) N
      = deningerHarmonicPartial N := rfl

/-- **Abel summation for the Dirichlet series.**  The `n = 0` increment is killed by `μ(0) = 0`, so
the remaining sum is the Abel average of the shifted partial sums. -/
theorem deningerDirichlet_abelSum {σ : ℝ} (N : ℕ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (N + 2), deningerDirichletTerm σ n)
      = deningerHarmonicPartial (N + 1) * (((N : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-σ))
        + ∑ m ∈ Finset.range N, deningerHarmonicPartial (m + 1) * deningerAbelWeight σ m := by
  have habel := deningerAbelSummation
    (fun n : ℕ => ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) (fun n : ℕ => ((n : ℝ) ^ (-σ))) (N + 1)
  have hterm : ∀ n : ℕ, ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) ^ (-σ))
      = deningerDirichletTerm σ n := fun n => rfl
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun n _ => hterm n)] at habel
  rw [habel, deningerHarmonicPartial_eq]
  have hcast : (((N + 1 : ℕ)) : ℝ) = (N : ℝ) + 1 := by push_cast; ring
  rw [hcast]
  congr 1
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ']
  have hzero : deningerPartialSum (fun n : ℕ => ((moebius n : ℤ) : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) 0 *
      (((0 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-σ) - ((0 + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ (-σ)) = 0 := by
    rw [deningerPartialSum_zero]
    simp
  rw [hzero, add_zero]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun m _ => ?_
  rw [deningerHarmonicPartial_eq, deningerAbelWeight]
  congr 2 <;> push_cast <;> ring

end

end RHTower

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.DeningerMobiusAbel
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.DeningerLogPullDeriv

/-!
# The Abel coefficient sequence

Integrating one Abel difference against `dx` produces the coefficient `1/(i(i+1))`: the set of
dilations carrying a fixed point `u` into the `i`-th window is the interval `[u/(i+1), u/i]`, of
length `u/(i(i+1))`.

Summing those coefficients against the summatory function is therefore controlled by the same
inverse-square series that the unconditional Möbius saving already gives.

* `deningerAbelWindow_volume` : the window has length `u/(i(i+1))`.
* `deningerAbelCoefficient_summable` : **`∑_i |M(i)|/(i(i+1)) < ∞`.**
-/

namespace RHTower

open MeasureTheory

noncomputable section

/-- **The dilation window.**  For `u > 0` and `i ≥ 1`, the dilations carrying `u` into the `i`-th
Abel window form the interval `[u/(i+1), u/i]`, whose length is `u/(i(i+1))`. -/
theorem deningerAbelWindow_volume {i : ℕ} (hi : 0 < i) (u : ℝ) :
    {x : ℝ | (i : ℝ) * x ≤ u ∧ u ≤ ((i : ℝ) + 1) * x}
      = Set.Icc (u / ((i : ℝ) + 1)) (u / (i : ℝ)) := by
  have hir : (0 : ℝ) < (i : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hi
  have hi1 : (0 : ℝ) < (i : ℝ) + 1 := by linarith
  ext x
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [div_le_iff₀ hi1, mul_comm]
      exact h2
    · rw [le_div_iff₀ hir, mul_comm]
      exact h1
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · have hx := (le_div_iff₀ hir).mp h2
      rw [mul_comm]
      exact hx
    · have hx := (div_le_iff₀ hi1).mp h1
      rw [mul_comm]
      exact hx

/-- The length of the dilation window. -/
theorem deningerAbelWindow_length {i : ℕ} (hi : 0 < i) (u : ℝ) :
    u / (i : ℝ) - u / ((i : ℝ) + 1) = u / ((i : ℝ) * ((i : ℝ) + 1)) := by
  have hir : (0 : ℝ) < (i : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hi
  have hi1 : (0 : ℝ) < (i : ℝ) + 1 := by linarith
  field_simp
  ring

/-- **The Abel coefficient sequence is summable.**  The coefficients `1/(i(i+1))` are dominated by
`1/i²`, so the unconditional saving already controls them. -/
theorem deningerAbelCoefficient_summable :
    Summable fun i : ℕ => |Sieve.mertensM i| / ((i : ℝ) * ((i : ℝ) + 1)) := by
  refine Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun i => ?_) (fun i => ?_)
    deningerMertensM_invSq_summable
  · rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos i with rfl | hi
    · simp
    · have hir : (0 : ℝ) < (i : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hi
      positivity
  · rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos i with rfl | hi
    · simp
    · have hir : (0 : ℝ) < (i : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hi
      have hsq : (i : ℝ) ^ 2 ≤ (i : ℝ) * ((i : ℝ) + 1) := by nlinarith
      refine div_le_div_of_nonneg_left (abs_nonneg _) (by positivity) hsq
end

end RHTower

/-! ## The window as a measurable set of the plane -/

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory

/-- **The measure of the dilation window.** -/
theorem deningerAbelWindow_measure {i : ℕ} (hi : 0 < i) (u : ℝ) :
    volume {x : ℝ | (i : ℝ) * x ≤ u ∧ u ≤ ((i : ℝ) + 1) * x}
      = ENNReal.ofReal (u / ((i : ℝ) * ((i : ℝ) + 1))) := by
  rw [deningerAbelWindow_volume hi u, Real.volume_Icc, deningerAbelWindow_length hi u]

/-- The window, as a set of the plane, is measurable: it is cut out by two closed conditions. -/
theorem deningerAbelWindow_measurableSet (i : ℕ) :
    MeasurableSet {p : ℝ × ℝ | (i : ℝ) * p.1 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.2 ≤ ((i : ℝ) + 1) * p.1} := by
  have h1 : MeasurableSet {p : ℝ × ℝ | (i : ℝ) * p.1 ≤ p.2} :=
    measurableSet_le (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
  have h2 : MeasurableSet {p : ℝ × ℝ | p.2 ≤ ((i : ℝ) + 1) * p.1} :=
    measurableSet_le (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
  exact h1.inter h2

end

end RHTower
